name: .codex/agents/<name>.toml
description: Define a reusable Codex subagent role in project scope.

examples.explanation: Create a focused worker with its own instructions and tool policy.

when_to_use: Create a focused worker with its own instructions and tool policy.

name: codex
description: Start Codex interactively, optionally with an initial prompt.
when_to_use: Use this control when start Codex interactively, optionally with an initial prompt.

examples.explanation: Start an interactive session with a prompt.

name: --add-dir
description: Grant Codex write access to an additional directory while retaining the selected sandbox mode.

examples.explanation: Allow work in a sibling shared library without disabling sandboxing.

when_to_use: Use when a task legitimately spans directories outside the primary workspace.
when_not_to_use: Grant only the narrow directories required by the task.

name: --ask-for-approval
description: Set the approval policy to untrusted, on-request, or never.
when_to_use: Use this control when set the approval policy to untrusted, on-request, or never.

examples.explanation: Prompt for approval when Codex requests escalation.

name: --bundled
description: Skip refreshing the model catalog and print only the catalog bundled with the current Codex binary.

examples.explanation: Inspect only models shipped with the current installation.

conditions: Used with codex debug models.

name: --cd
description: Set the working directory for the Codex invocation.

examples.explanation: Start Codex with services/api as its working directory.

when_to_use: Use when invoking Codex from outside the repository or resuming work in a different current directory.

name: --config
description: Override a config.toml value for the current invocation using a dotted key and TOML value.

examples.explanation: Use high reasoning effort for one invocation without changing config.toml.

when_to_use: Use for a temporary override that should take precedence over configuration files.
when_not_to_use: Use config.toml instead for a setting that should persist across sessions.

name: --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
description: Disable approval prompts and sandbox restrictions for the invocation.

examples.explanation: Run without Codex approval or sandbox protections inside an already isolated disposable environment.

when_to_use: Use only inside a dedicated external sandbox or disposable virtual machine.
when_not_to_use: Do not use on a normal workstation or repository when workspace-write plus targeted approvals is sufficient.

conditions: Managed policy can prevent unrestricted execution.

name: --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust
description: Run enabled hooks without requiring persisted hook trust for this invocation.

examples.explanation: Use only in automation that has already vetted every enabled hook source.

when_to_use: Use only in controlled automation where hook sources are already trusted externally.
when_not_to_use: Do not use for ordinary local development or with unreviewed hooks.

conditions: Intended for automation that already vets hook sources.

name: --disable
description: Force-disable a named Codex feature flag for this invocation. Repeat the option to disable multiple features.

examples.explanation: Start Codex with shell snapshots disabled for this invocation.

when_to_use: Test behavior without a feature while leaving persisted configuration unchanged.

name: --download-url
description: Override the ChatGPT desktop app installer URL used by codex app when installation is required.

examples.explanation: Use a controlled installer endpoint during desktop-app setup.

conditions: Advanced override for codex app installation.

name: --enable
description: Force-enable a named Codex feature flag for this invocation. Repeat the option to enable multiple features.

examples.explanation: Start Codex with shell snapshots enabled for this invocation.

when_to_use: Test or temporarily activate a documented feature without changing persisted configuration.

name: --full-auto
description: Apply the documented low-friction preset for automatic work within sandbox boundaries.

examples.command: codex --full-auto "run the test suite and fix failures"
examples.explanation: Let Codex iterate automatically while remaining subject to the preset's sandbox constraints.

when_to_use: Use for well-scoped local work where automatic iteration is appropriate.
when_not_to_use: Do not confuse this preset with unrestricted host access.

name: --image
description: Attach one or more local image paths to the initial prompt. Supply comma-separated paths or repeat the option.

examples.explanation: Attach a screenshot to the opening prompt.

when_to_use: Include screenshots, diagrams, or other local images in the initial request.

name: --local-provider
description: Select the local provider used with --oss. Documented values are lmstudio and ollama.

examples.explanation: Run with a local model served by Ollama.

when_to_use: Choose which supported local provider backs an OSS-model session.

conditions: Requires --oss and a running supported local provider.

name: --model
description: Select the model for the Codex invocation.
when_to_use: Use this control when select the model for the Codex invocation.

examples.explanation: Start with a selected model.

name: --no-alt-screen
description: Run the TUI without the terminal alternate-screen buffer, overriding tui.alternate_screen for the invocation.

examples.explanation: Keep Codex output in normal terminal scrollback.

when_to_use: Preserve terminal scrollback or work around alternate-screen behavior in a terminal multiplexer.

name: --oss
description: Use a locally served open-source model, with the provider selected from configuration or --local-provider.

examples.explanation: Start a local-model Codex session with an initial prompt.

when_to_use: Run Codex against a configured supported local model provider.

conditions: Requires a running supported local model provider.

name: --profile
description: Layer the named profile configuration from the Codex home directory onto the invocation.

examples.explanation: Start Codex using the review profile.

when_to_use: Switch between reusable configuration sets without editing the base config.

conditions: The named profile must exist in the Codex home directory.

name: --remote
description: Connect the CLI to a Codex app-server endpoint using ws, wss, or a Unix socket endpoint.

examples.explanation: Connect to an app server listening on the local port documented by the app-server example.

when_to_use: Run the CLI as a client of an existing Codex app server.

conditions: Requires an accessible Codex app-server endpoint.

name: --remote-auth-token-env
description: Read the bearer token for a --remote app-server connection from the named environment variable.

examples.explanation: Pass a locally exported token through an environment variable rather than the command line.

when_to_use: Authenticate a remote app-server connection without placing the token directly in the command line.

conditions: Requires --remote; supported with wss endpoints and local ws endpoints.

name: --sandbox
description: Select read-only, workspace-write, or danger-full-access sandboxing.
when_to_use: Use this control when select read-only, workspace-write, or danger-full-access sandboxing.

examples.explanation: Allow writes within the workspace sandbox.

name: --search
description: Switch Codex web search from its cached default to live browsing for the invocation.

examples.command: codex --search "verify the current release notes for this dependency"
examples.explanation: Use live web results for a time-sensitive task.

when_to_use: Use when freshness matters and cached search could be stale.
when_not_to_use: Do not use web search when the task must rely exclusively on repository content.

conditions: Requires web search availability and network access.

name: --strict-config
description: Error when config.toml contains fields that this Codex version does not recognize.

examples.explanation: Fail fast in CI when configuration contains an unsupported field.

when_to_use: Validate configuration compatibility during upgrades or automated runs.

conditions: Supported by documented runtime commands including codex, exec, review, resume, fork, app-server, mcp-server, and exec-server.

name: codex app
description: Launch the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS or Windows. On macOS, Codex can open a workspace path; on Windows, it prints the path to open.

examples.explanation: Open the current workspace in the Codex desktop app.

conditions: Desktop-app behavior varies by operating system.

name: codex app-server
description: Launch the local Codex app server over JSONL standard I/O, WebSocket, or a Unix socket for client integrations and debugging.

examples.explanation: Start the app server with its default JSONL standard-I/O transport.
Expose a local WebSocket endpoint for an app-server client.

when_to_use: Use when developing or debugging a client that speaks the Codex app-server protocol.
when_not_to_use: Do not expose an unencrypted ws:// listener beyond localhost or a trusted tunnel.

conditions: Primarily intended for development and debugging and may change.

name: codex apply
description: Apply the most recent diff from a Codex cloud chat to the local repository with git apply.

examples.explanation: Bring an authenticated cloud task's completed patch into the checked-out repository for local review and testing.

when_to_use: Use after a cloud task has produced a diff that you want to inspect locally.
when_not_to_use: Do not use with uncommitted local changes unless you are prepared to resolve apply conflicts.

conditions: Requires authentication and access to the cloud chat.

name: codex archive
description: Archive a saved interactive session by session ID or session name.

examples.explanation: Archive a saved session by its identifier.

name: codex cloud
description: Open the cloud-chat picker, submit a task, or list recent Codex cloud chats.

examples.explanation: Open the interactive cloud-chat picker.
List recent cloud tasks in machine-readable form for automation.

when_to_use: Use to submit or inspect Codex cloud work from the terminal.

conditions: Requires Codex cloud access and authentication.

name: codex completion
description: Generate a completion script for a supported shell.

examples.explanation: Print the zsh completion script.
Generate Bash completions for installation in the shell's completion directory.

when_to_use: Use to enable tab completion for Codex commands and options.

name: codex debug app-server send-message-v2
description: Send one message through the app-server V2 thread and turn flow using the built-in test client.

examples.explanation: Exercise the app-server message flow while diagnosing protocol behavior.

conditions: This built-in debug flow is experimental.

name: codex debug models
description: Print the raw model catalog Codex sees, optionally limiting output to the catalog bundled with the current binary.

examples.explanation: Inspect the model catalog shipped with the installed binary.

conditions: This diagnostic command is experimental.

name: codex debug prompt-input
description: Render the exact model-visible prompt input list as JSON, optionally with a prompt and images.

examples.command: codex debug prompt-input "Explain the current task"
examples.explanation: Inspect the prompt context Codex will send to the model.

conditions: This diagnostic command is experimental.

name: codex delete
description: Permanently delete a saved interactive session by session ID or session name.

examples.explanation: Remove a saved session that is no longer needed.

conditions: Deletion is permanent.

name: codex doctor
description: Generate a local diagnostic report covering installation, configuration, authentication, runtime, Git, terminal, app-server, and thread health.

examples.explanation: Capture a health report before filing a support issue for a broken CLI installation.

when_to_use: Use when Codex startup, authentication, Git integration, or terminal behavior is failing unexpectedly.

name: codex exec
description: Run a prompt non-interactively, accepting the prompt argument or standard input.
when_to_use: Use this control when run a prompt non-interactively, accepting the prompt argument or standard input.

examples.explanation: Run one headless task.

name: codex execpolicy
description: Evaluate execpolicy rule files and see whether a command would be allowed, prompted, or blocked.

examples.explanation: Inspect the installed policy-evaluation syntax before checking a command in an experimental release.

conditions: Execpolicy is experimental and may change.

name: codex features
description: List, enable, or disable feature flags persisted in CODEX_HOME/config.toml.

examples.explanation: List feature flags and their current state.
Persistently enable a documented feature for future sessions.

when_to_use: Use to inspect or deliberately opt into a named Codex feature.
when_not_to_use: Do not enable an unfamiliar experimental feature without checking its official documentation and maturity.

conditions: Individual features can have their own maturity and availability.

name: codex fork
description: Fork a prior interactive session into a new chat, using the picker or the most recent session.

examples.explanation: Choose a session to fork.
Branch the most recent session while preserving its original history.

when_to_use: Use when you want to explore a different approach without altering the original session lineage.

name: codex login
description: Authenticate Codex through supported account or token flows.
when_to_use: Use this control when authenticate Codex through supported account or token flows.

examples.explanation: Start interactive authentication.

name: codex logout
description: Clear stored Codex authentication.
when_to_use: Use this control when clear stored Codex authentication.

examples.explanation: Sign out of Codex.

name: codex mcp
description: Manage Codex MCP server configurations.
when_to_use: Use this control when manage Codex MCP server configurations.

examples.explanation: List configured MCP servers.

name: codex mcp-server
display_name: Run Codex as an MCP server
description: Run Codex as an MCP server over stdio.

examples.explanation: Start the legacy stdio MCP server interface.

conditions: Deprecated; use the Codex app server instead.

name: codex plugin
description: Install, list, and remove plugins from configured marketplace sources.

examples.explanation: List plugins available from configured marketplaces.

name: codex plugin marketplace
description: Add, list, upgrade, or remove plugin marketplaces from Git or local sources.

examples.explanation: Inspect configured plugin marketplace sources.

name: codex remote-control
description: Run or manage remote control for the local app server, or create a short-lived pairing code.

examples.explanation: Start the documented remote-control flow for a local app server.

conditions: Remote control is experimental.

name: codex resume
description: Resume a prior Codex session by identifier or picker selection.
when_to_use: Use this control when resume a prior Codex session by identifier or picker selection.

examples.explanation: Choose a session to resume.

name: codex review
description: Review uncommitted, branch, or commit changes.
when_to_use: Use this control when review uncommitted, branch, or commit changes.

examples.explanation: Review current uncommitted changes.

name: codex sandbox
display_name: Run a command in a Codex sandbox
description: Run arbitrary commands inside a Codex-provided macOS, Linux, or Windows sandbox.

examples.explanation: Run a diagnostic command inside the macOS sandbox.

name: codex unarchive
description: Restore an archived interactive session by session ID or session name.

examples.explanation: Restore an archived session so it can be resumed.

name: codex update
description: Update Codex CLI to the latest available version.
when_to_use: Use this control when update Codex CLI to the latest available version.

examples.explanation: Install the latest CLI release.

name: $CODEX_HOME/config.toml
description: Primary Codex user configuration file; CODEX_HOME defaults to ~/.codex.

name: agents
description: Multi-agent settings and custom role declarations. Scalar setting names are reserved and can't be used as custom role names.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents behavior.

name: agents.<name>.config_file
description: Path to a TOML config layer for that role; relative paths resolve from the config file that declares the role.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.<name>.config_file behavior.

name: agents.<name>.description
description: Role guidance shown to Codex when choosing and spawning that agent type.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.<name>.description behavior.

name: agents.default_subagent_model
description: Default model for spawned agents. An explicit spawn model takes precedence.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.default_subagent_model behavior.

name: agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort
description: Default reasoning effort for spawned agents. An explicit spawn effort takes precedence.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort behavior.

name: agents.enabled
description: Enable or disable multi-agent tools (default: true).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.enabled behavior.

name: agents.interrupt_message
description: Record a model-visible message when an agent turn is interrupted (default: true).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.interrupt_message behavior.

name: agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session
description: Maximum number of spawned-agent threads that can be open concurrently, excluding the primary thread. When unset, Codex chooses the default.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session behavior.

name: agents.max_threads
description: Legacy alias for agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agents.max_threads behavior.
when_not_to_use: Avoid this deprecated setting in new configuration; use the documented replacement when available.

name: allow_appshots
description: Set to false to disable Appshots for managed users. If omitted, Appshots remain unconstrained by requirements and follow normal product availability.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allow_appshots behavior.

name: allow_login_shell
description: Enforce whether shell tools can start a login shell.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allow_login_shell behavior.

name: allow_managed_hooks_only
description: When true, Codex skips user, project, session, and plugin hooks while still allowing managed hooks from requirements.toml and other managed config layers.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allow_managed_hooks_only behavior.

name: allow_remote_control
description: Set to false to disable device remote control for managed users. If omitted, device remote control remains unconstrained by requirements and follows normal product availability.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allow_remote_control behavior.

name: allowed_approval_policies
description: Allowed values for approval_policy (for example untrusted, on-request, never, and granular).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowed_approval_policies behavior.

name: allowed_approvals_reviewers
description: Allowed values for approvals_reviewer, such as user and auto_review.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowed_approvals_reviewers behavior.

name: allowed_permission_profiles
description: Complete list of allowed permission profiles. Profiles set to true are allowed. Profiles that are omitted or set to false are denied, including profiles added in future versions. When requirements sources are combined, entries are matched by profile name.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowed_permission_profiles behavior.

name: allowed_permission_profiles.<name>
description: Allow or deny a built-in or custom permission profile defined in a loaded config or requirements source. A later, higher-precedence requirements source can use false to turn off a profile allowed by an earlier, lower-precedence source.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowed_permission_profiles.<name> behavior.

name: allowed_sandbox_modes
description: Allowed values for sandbox_mode.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowed_sandbox_modes behavior.

name: allowed_web_search_modes
description: Allowed values for web_search (disabled, cached, indexed, live). disabled is always allowed; an empty list effectively allows only disabled.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowed_web_search_modes behavior.

name: analytics.enabled
description: Enable or disable analytics for this machine/profile. When unset, the client default applies.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented analytics.enabled behavior.

name: approval_policy
description: Control when Codex pauses for approval before executing commands; granular policy objects can handle prompt categories separately.

examples.explanation: Let Codex request approval when an operation needs escalation.

when_to_use: Use in config.toml to set a persistent approval default instead of passing --ask-for-approval each time.

conditions: Managed requirements can restrict allowed values.

notes: The on-failure value is deprecated; official guidance is on-request for interactive runs or never for non-interactive runs.

name: approval_policy.granular.mcp_elicitations
description: When true, MCP elicitation prompts are allowed to surface instead of being auto-rejected.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented approval_policy.granular.mcp_elicitations behavior.

name: approval_policy.granular.request_permissions
description: When true, prompts from the request_permissions tool are allowed to surface.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented approval_policy.granular.request_permissions behavior.

name: approval_policy.granular.rules
description: When true, approvals triggered by execpolicy prompt rules are allowed to surface.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented approval_policy.granular.rules behavior.

name: approval_policy.granular.sandbox_approval
description: When true, sandbox escalation approval prompts are allowed to surface.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented approval_policy.granular.sandbox_approval behavior.

name: approval_policy.granular.skill_approval
description: When true, skill-script approval prompts are allowed to surface.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented approval_policy.granular.skill_approval behavior.

name: approvals_reviewer
description: Who reviews eligible approval prompts under on-request or granular approval policies. Defaults to user; auto_review uses the reviewer subagent. This setting doesn't change sandboxing or review actions already allowed inside the sandbox.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented approvals_reviewer behavior.

name: apps
description: Managed app requirements keyed by app identifier. Requirements can disable an app or constrain approval behavior for individual tools.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps behavior.

name: apps.<id>.approvals_reviewer
description: Reviewer for this app's tool approval prompts. Overrides apps._default.approvals_reviewer.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.approvals_reviewer behavior.

name: apps.<id>.default_tools_approval_mode
description: Default approval behavior for tools in this app unless a per-tool override exists.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.default_tools_approval_mode behavior.

name: apps.<id>.default_tools_enabled
description: Default enabled state for tools in this app unless a per-tool override exists.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.default_tools_enabled behavior.

name: apps.<id>.destructive_enabled
description: Allow or block tools in this app that advertise destructive_hint = true.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.destructive_enabled behavior.

name: apps.<id>.enabled
description: Set to false to disable an app. A disabled requirement remains restrictive when multiple requirements sources are merged.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.enabled behavior.

name: apps.<id>.open_world_enabled
description: Allow or block tools in this app that advertise open_world_hint = true.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.open_world_enabled behavior.

name: apps.<id>.tools.<tool>.approval_mode
description: Set the managed approval mode for one app tool.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.tools.<tool>.approval_mode behavior.

name: apps.<id>.tools.<tool>.enabled
description: Per-tool enabled override for an app tool (for example repos/list).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps.<id>.tools.<tool>.enabled behavior.

name: apps._default.approvals_reviewer
description: Default reviewer for app tool approval prompts unless overridden per app. When omitted, apps inherit the top-level approvals_reviewer value.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps._default.approvals_reviewer behavior.

name: apps._default.default_tools_approval_mode
description: Default approval behavior for app tools without per-app or per-tool overrides.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps._default.default_tools_approval_mode behavior.

name: apps._default.destructive_enabled
description: Default allow/deny for app tools with destructive_hint = true.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps._default.destructive_enabled behavior.

name: apps._default.enabled
description: Default app enabled state for all apps unless overridden per app.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps._default.enabled behavior.

name: apps._default.open_world_enabled
description: Default allow/deny for app tools with open_world_hint = true.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apps._default.open_world_enabled behavior.

name: auto_review.policy
description: Local Markdown policy instructions for automatic review. Managed guardian_policy_config takes precedence. Blank values are ignored.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented auto_review.policy behavior.

name: background_terminal_max_timeout
description: Maximum poll window in milliseconds for empty write_stdin polls (background terminal polling). Default: 300000 (5 minutes). Replaces the older background_terminal_timeout key.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented background_terminal_max_timeout behavior.

name: chatgpt_base_url
description: Override the base URL used during the ChatGPT login flow.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented chatgpt_base_url behavior.

name: check_for_update_on_startup
description: Enforce whether Codex checks for updates when it starts.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented check_for_update_on_startup behavior.

name: cli_auth_credentials_store
description: Control where the CLI stores cached credentials (file-based auth.json vs OS keychain).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented cli_auth_credentials_store behavior.

name: compact_prompt
description: Inline override for the history compaction prompt.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented compact_prompt behavior.

name: computer_use
description: Computer Use requirements enforced from requirements.toml.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented computer_use behavior.

name: computer_use.allow_locked_computer_use
description: Set to false to prevent Computer Use from operating after a managed macOS device locks. If omitted, locked use remains unconstrained by requirements.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented computer_use.allow_locked_computer_use behavior.

name: computer_use.windows.always_allowed_app_ids
description: Windows app identifiers that Computer Use can open without prompting. Apps not in the list require approval; remove saved entries from the ChatGPT desktop app's Computer Use settings.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented computer_use.windows.always_allowed_app_ids behavior.

name: default_permissions
description: Managed default permission profile. The profile must be allowed by allowed_permission_profiles. Set this explicitly for predictable behavior; if omitted, Codex defaults to :workspace only when both :workspace and :read-only are explicitly allowed.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented default_permissions behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>
description: User-level only. Defines an additional Open in target for the ChatGPT desktop app. See Add custom file handlers for examples and handler ID constraints.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id> behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.args
description: Arguments inserted between the command and file input (default: []).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.args behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.command
description: Executable path or command name to detect and launch. Required.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.command behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.icon
description: Bundled asset path, Base64-encoded data:image/... URL, file URI, or absolute local path for the handler icon. Required; unsupported sources use the default VS Code icon.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.icon behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.input
description: How the app sends file input to the handler (default: path).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.input behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.label
description: Display name shown in Open in menus. Required.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.label behavior.

name: desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.supports_ssh
description: Offer the handler for files in SSH workspaces (default: false).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktop.custom_file_handlers.<id>.supports_ssh behavior.

name: developer_instructions
description: Additional developer instructions injected into the session (optional).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented developer_instructions behavior.

name: disable_paste_burst
description: Disable burst-paste detection in the TUI.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disable_paste_burst behavior.

name: enforce_residency
description: Require Codex service traffic to use a supported data residency. Currently accepts us.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enforce_residency behavior.

name: experimental_compact_prompt_file
description: Load the compaction prompt override from a file (experimental).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented experimental_compact_prompt_file behavior.

name: experimental_network
description: Administrator-managed network requirements for sandboxed local commands, enforced from requirements.toml. When enabled, these requirements can start the command network proxy without features.network_proxy. They do not control web search, apps, MCP servers, browsers, or Codex cloud networking.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented experimental_network behavior.

name: experimental_network.allow_local_binding
description: Permit broader local/private-network access for sandboxed networking. Exact local IP literal or localhost allow rules can still permit specific local targets when this stays false.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented experimental_network.allow_local_binding behavior.

name: experimental_network.allow_upstream_proxy
description: Allow sandboxed networking to chain through an upstream proxy from the environment.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented experimental_network.allow_upstream_proxy behavior.

name: experimental_network.allowed_domains

name: permissions
description: Admin-defined permission profiles keyed by profile name. Uses the same profile fields as config.toml.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions behavior.

name: permissions.<name>
description: Admin-defined permission profile. The name can't start with :, use the reserved name filesystem, or duplicate a profile from a loaded config. Uses the same profile fields as config.toml; see the Permissions guide for the complete profile schema.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name> behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.description
description: Human-readable description for this named profile. A profile does not inherit its parent's description through extends.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.description behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.extends
description: Optional parent profile applied before this named profile. Set it to another named profile, :read-only, or :workspace; :danger-full-access, undefined parents, and cycles are rejected.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.extends behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.filesystem
description: Named filesystem permission profile. Each key is an absolute path or special token such as :minimal or :workspace_roots.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.filesystem behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.filesystem.<path-or-glob>
description: Grant direct access for a path, glob pattern, or special token, or scope nested entries under that root. Use "deny" to deny reads for matching paths.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.filesystem.<path-or-glob> behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.filesystem.glob_scan_max_depth
description: Maximum depth for expanding deny-read glob patterns on platforms that snapshot matches before sandbox startup. Must be at least 1 when set.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.filesystem.glob_scan_max_depth behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.allow_local_binding
description: Permit broader local/private-network access through sandboxed networking. Exact local IP literal or localhost allow rules can still permit specific local targets when this stays false.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.allow_local_binding behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.allow_upstream_proxy
description: Allow sandboxed networking to chain through another upstream proxy.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.allow_upstream_proxy behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets
description: Allow arbitrary Unix socket destinations instead of the default restricted set. Use only in tightly controlled environments.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy
description: Permit non-loopback bind addresses for sandboxed networking listeners. Enabling it can expose listeners beyond localhost.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.domains
description: Domain rules for sandboxed commands. Enforced only when features.network_proxy or enabled administrator-managed networking requirements activate the proxy. Supports exact hosts, *.example.com, .example.com, and global * allow rules; deny wins. Does not restrict web search, apps, or MCP servers.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.domains behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.domains.<pattern>
description: Allow or deny an exact host or scoped wildcard pattern such as *.example.com or .example.com.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.domains.<pattern> behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5
description: Expose SOCKS5 support when this permissions profile enables sandboxed networking.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5 behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5_udp
description: Allow UDP over the SOCKS5 listener when enabled.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.enable_socks5_udp behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.enabled
description: Enable network access for commands in this permission profile. This does not start the network proxy. Without features.network_proxy or enabled administrator-managed networking requirements, command network access is direct and profile domain rules are not enforced.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.enabled behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.mode
description: Network proxy mode used for subprocess traffic.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.mode behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.proxy_url
description: HTTP listener URL used when this permissions profile enables sandboxed networking.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.proxy_url behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.socks_url
description: SOCKS5 proxy endpoint used by this permissions profile.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.socks_url behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets
description: Unix socket allowlist overrides for sandboxed networking. Use socket paths as keys; allow adds a path, and deny rejects it.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets.<path>
description: Add an absolute Unix socket path to the effective allowlist with allow, or reject it with deny. Denied entries are omitted from the effective allowlist.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.network.unix_sockets.<path> behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.workspace_roots

when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.workspace_roots behavior.

name: permissions.<name>.workspace_roots.<path>
description: Opt a path into the profile's workspace root set when true. Disabled entries remain inactive.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.<name>.workspace_roots.<path> behavior.

name: permissions.filesystem.deny_read
description: Admin-enforced filesystem read denials. Entries can be paths or glob patterns, and users cannot weaken them with local config.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.filesystem.deny_read behavior.

description: Pick which model answers when Claude calls the server-side advisor tool. Unset it to turn the advisor off. The advisor must be at least as capable as your main model; when it isn't, Claude Code sends requests without the advisor. See Choose an advisor model.

when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented advisorModel behavior.

name: agent
description: Run the main thread as a named subagent, so Claude Code applies that subagent's system prompt, tool restrictions, and model to your session. The same key sets the default agent for sessions you dispatch from claude agents.
syntax: agent: <string, the name of a built-in or custom agent>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agent behavior.

name: agentPushNotifEnabled
description: Allow Claude to send a push notification to your phone when it decides one is worth sending, for example when a long task finishes. Claude Code syncs this choice to your account, and pushes arrive while Remote Control is connected. Appears in /config as Push when Claude decides.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented agentPushNotifEnabled behavior.

name: allowAllClaudeAiMcps
description: Load the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json. Without this key, managed-mcp.json takes exclusive control of MCP servers and suppresses those connectors.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowAllClaudeAiMcps behavior.

name: allowManagedHooksOnly
description: Restrict hook execution to hooks your organization deploys.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowManagedHooksOnly behavior.

name: allowManagedMcpServersOnly
description: Make the managed allowlist the only one that applies. Claude Code then reads allowedMcpServers from managed settings alone and ignores allowlists in user, project, and local settings; deniedMcpServers still merges from every file, so users can still block servers for themselves. Administrators set it so a user's own settings can't broaden what the managed allowlist permits.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowManagedMcpServersOnly behavior.

name: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
description: Make managed settings the only source of allow, ask, and deny permission rules. Claude Code then ignores rules in user, project, local, and --settings files, ignores --allowedTools, hides the always-allow choices in permission prompts, and stops saving new rules. When parent settings from an embedding host apply, Claude Code treats them as part of the managed tier: it keeps their deny and ask rules and drops their allow rules and additionalDirectories.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly behavior.

name: allowedChannelPlugins
description: Choose which channel plugins can push messages into sessions in your organization. When you set it, Claude Code uses your list in place of the default Anthropic allowlist; each entry names a plugin and the marketplace it comes from.
syntax: allowedChannelPlugins: <array of objects, each with marketplace and plugin strings>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowedChannelPlugins behavior.

name: allowedHttpHookUrls
description: Limit which URLs HTTP hooks can target. When you define this key, Claude Code runs an HTTP hook only if its URL matches one of the patterns and blocks the rest without running them; an empty array blocks every HTTP hook.
syntax: allowedHttpHookUrls: <array of URL patterns, with * as a wildcard>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowedHttpHookUrls behavior.

name: allowedMcpServers
description: Allowlist the MCP servers people can use. Claude Code blocks any server that doesn't match an entry wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers passed with --mcp-config, and servers from managed-mcp.json. Built-in servers such as Claude in Chrome, the ide server Claude Code connects to in a running VS Code or JetBrains IDE, and servers the CLI itself configures are exempt from the allowlist, and the denylist still applies to them. In-process type: "sdk" servers, which the app that started the session registers, are exempt from both lists.
syntax: allowedMcpServers: <array of objects, each with exactly one key: serverName, a string limited to letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores; serverCommand, an array of the command and its arguments matched exactly; or serverUrl, a URL pattern with * wildcards>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented allowedMcpServers behavior.

name: alwaysThinkingEnabled
description: Turn extended thinking off for every session by setting this to false. Thinking is on by default, so true changes nothing. Most people set this through /config rather than by editing the file.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented alwaysThinkingEnabled behavior.

name: apiKeyHelper
description: Run your own command to produce the credential Claude Code sends with model requests. Claude Code runs the command through the system shell, /bin/sh on macOS and Linux and cmd on Windows, and sends its output as both the X-Api-Key and Authorization: Bearer headers. Use it for dynamic or rotating credentials, such as short-lived tokens fetched from a vault.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented apiKeyHelper behavior.

name: askUserQuestionTimeout
description: Let an unanswered AskUserQuestion dialog auto-continue after a period of idle time, submitting whatever options you had already selected. Set it when you step away and want Claude to continue without you. With the default, questions wait until you answer them. Requires Claude Code v2.1.200 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented askUserQuestionTimeout behavior.

conditions: Let an unanswered AskUserQuestion dialog auto-continue after a period of idle time, submitting whatever options you had already selected. name: autoMode
description: Add your own rules to what the auto mode classifier blocks and allows. Use it to tell the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains your organization trusts, so it stops blocking routine internal operations. The classifier ships with built-in allow and deny rules. Include the literal string "$defaults" in an array to keep those built-in rules at that position and add yours around them; leave it out to replace them with yours.
syntax: autoMode: <object with environment, allow, soft_deny, and hard_deny arrays of prose rules, plus the classifyAllShell Boolean>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented autoMode behavior.

name: autoMode.classifyAllShell
description: Send every Bash and PowerShell command through the auto mode classifier while auto mode is active. By default, auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code: tool-wide and wildcard rules such as Bash(*), and interpreter or shell-wrapper prefixes such as Bash(python *). A command that any other allow rule matches, such as Bash(npm test), skips the classifier, and a destructive argument the rule's prefix didn't anticipate can get through unseen. Setting this key suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every command. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented autoMode.classifyAllShell behavior.

conditions: Send every Bash and PowerShell command through the auto mode classifier while auto mode is active. By default, auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code: tool-wide and wildcard rules such as Bash(*), and interpreter or shell-wrapper prefixes such as Bash(python *). A command that any other allow rule matches, such as Bash(npm test), skips the classifier, and a destructive argument the rule's prefix didn't anticipate can get through unseen. Setting this key suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every command. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.

name: autoScrollEnabled
description: Follow new output to the bottom of the conversation in fullscreen rendering. Turn it off to stay where you scrolled while Claude keeps working; permission prompts still scroll into view.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented autoScrollEnabled behavior.

name: autoUpdatesChannel
description: Choose which release channel background auto-updates and claude update follow. Set "stable" for a version that is typically about one week old and skips releases with major regressions, or "latest" for the most recent release.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented autoUpdatesChannel behavior.

name: availableModels
description: Restrict which models people can select for the main session, subagents, skills, and the advisor. A managed list constrains /model, --model, and the model key in a developer's own files; a model outside it can't be selected. On its own this doesn't touch the Default option; pair it with enforceAvailableModels for that.
syntax: availableModels: <array of model aliases or IDs>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented availableModels behavior.

name: awaySummaryEnabled
description: Show a one-line session recap when you return to the terminal after a few minutes away. Set it to false, or turn off Session recap in /config, to stop the recap.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented awaySummaryEnabled behavior.

name: awsAuthRefresh
description: Run your own command, such as aws sso login, to refresh the credentials in your .aws directory when the ones Claude Code has for Amazon Bedrock stop working. Claude Code checks the current credentials against STS first and runs the command only when that check fails, then reads the refreshed .aws directory.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented awsAuthRefresh behavior.

name: awsCredentialExport
description: Run your own command that prints AWS credentials as JSON, so Claude Code can call Amazon Bedrock with credentials that don't live in your .aws directory. Claude Code accepts the aws sts output shape and the flat aws configure export-credentials shape, and scopes the credentials to its own Bedrock client, so the shell commands Claude runs still see your ambient credentials.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented awsCredentialExport behavior.

name: axScreenReader
description: Render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Screen-reader mode uses the classic renderer, so the tui setting has no effect while it is active; attached background sessions still render fullscreen. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented axScreenReader behavior.

conditions: Render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Screen-reader mode uses the classic renderer, so the tui setting has no effect while it is active; attached background sessions still render fullscreen. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later.

name: blockedMarketplaces
description: Block plugin marketplace sources for your organization. Claude Code checks the blocklist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins either. Blocked sources are checked before download, so they never touch the filesystem.
syntax: blockedMarketplaces: <array of marketplace source objects, in the same forms as strictKnownMarketplaces>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented blockedMarketplaces behavior.

name: browserExternalPageTools
description: Stop Claude from using its tools to read or act on external pages in the desktop app's Browser pane. People in your organization can still open external sites themselves, and local dev server previews keep working with Claude's tools. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.
syntax: browserExternalPageTools: <string, "disabled"; the desktop app also accepts "disable", in either case>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented browserExternalPageTools behavior.

name: channelsEnabled
description: Allow channels for your organization. On claude.ai Team and Enterprise plans, Claude Code blocks channels until you set this to true. For Anthropic Console accounts that authenticate with an API key, channels are allowed by default. If your organization deploys managed settings, Claude Code blocks channels on those accounts too until you set this key to true.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented channelsEnabled behavior.

conditions: Allow channels for your organization. On claude.ai Team and Enterprise plans, Claude Code blocks channels until you set this to true. For Anthropic Console accounts that authenticate with an API key, channels are allowed by default. If your organization deploys managed settings, Claude Code blocks channels on those accounts too until you set this key to true.

name: claudeMd
description: Inject CLAUDE.md-style instructions as organization-managed memory without deploying a separate file. Claude Code loads the text as a managed memory entry ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md files.
syntax: claudeMd: <string, the text of a CLAUDE.md file; write it as you would the file, Markdown included, with line breaks as \n>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented claudeMd behavior.

name: claudeMdExcludes
description: Skip specific CLAUDE.md files when Claude Code loads memory. In a large monorepo, use it to skip CLAUDE.md files from other teams that aren't relevant to your work; Exclude irrelevant CLAUDE.md files in the large-codebases guide walks through that case. Patterns match against absolute file paths.
syntax: claudeMdExcludes: <array of strings, each a glob pattern or absolute path>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented claudeMdExcludes behavior.

name: cleanupPeriodDays
description: Set how many days Claude Code keeps session transcripts and other application data before deleting them. Claude Code runs the deletion as a background sweep after a session starts, as long as it can safely determine the retention period.
syntax: cleanupPeriodDays: <number of days, a whole number, minimum 1>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented cleanupPeriodDays behavior.

name: companyAnnouncements
description: Show your organization's announcements to users at startup. When you list more than one, Claude Code picks one at random for each session; on a person's very first launch it shows the first entry.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented companyAnnouncements behavior.

name: crossSessionInbound
description: Choose what this session does with messages arriving from your other Claude Code sessions. When no value applies, Claude Code decides per message from the two sessions' permission-mode classes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented crossSessionInbound behavior.

conditions: Choose what this session does with messages arriving from your other Claude Code sessions. When no value applies, Claude Code decides per message from the two sessions' permission-mode classes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

name: defaultShell
description: Choose whether Bash or PowerShell runs the shell commands you type with the ! prefix in the input box, the ones Claude Code runs directly and adds to the session.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented defaultShell behavior.

name: deniedMcpServers
description: Block specific MCP servers. Claude Code refuses to load a matching server wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers passed with --mcp-config, servers from managed-mcp.json, and the claude.ai connectors it fetches itself. In-process type: "sdk" servers, which the app that started the session registers, are exempt.
syntax: deniedMcpServers: <array of objects, each with exactly one key: serverName, any non-empty string, so a claude.ai connector's display name such as "claude.ai Slack" works; serverCommand, an array of the command and its arguments matched exactly; or serverUrl, a URL pattern with * wildcards>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented deniedMcpServers behavior.

name: desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays
description: Set an age limit in days for the transcripts of sessions you started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork. Without this key, Claude Code keeps those transcripts at any age. Claude Code deletes each one once it's older than both this limit and cleanupPeriodDays, so with cleanupPeriodDays at its default of 30, a value of 7 still keeps them 30 days. When managed settings set cleanupPeriodDays, that period applies instead and this key is ignored. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.
syntax: desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays: <number of days, a whole number, minimum 0>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays behavior.

conditions: Set an age limit in days for the transcripts of sessions you started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork. Without this key, Claude Code keeps those transcripts at any age. Claude Code deletes each one once it's older than both this limit and cleanupPeriodDays, so with cleanupPeriodDays at its default of 30, a value of 7 still keeps them 30 days. When managed settings set cleanupPeriodDays, that period applies instead and this key is ignored. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.

name: dialogExpiry
description: Set the deadline for dialogs Claude Code forwards to a remote client, such as a Remote Control or SDK host, for the approval dialog for a held cross-session message, and for the mid-session Fable 5 usage-credits consent prompt in a session that may have nobody at the terminal. When no answer arrives before the deadline, Claude Code cancels the dialog and continues with its no-action default. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
syntax: dialogExpiry: <string, one of "60s", "5m", "10m", or "never", which disables the deadline>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented dialogExpiry behavior.

conditions: Set the deadline for dialogs Claude Code forwards to a remote client, such as a Remote Control or SDK host, for the approval dialog for a held cross-session message, and for the mid-session Fable 5 usage-credits consent prompt in a session that may have nobody at the terminal. When no answer arrives before the deadline, Claude Code cancels the dialog and continues with its no-action default. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

name: diffTool
description: Choose where Claude Code shows the diff of an Edit or Write change it proposes when a VS Code or JetBrains IDE is connected: "auto" opens it in the IDE's diff viewer, "terminal" keeps it in the terminal. Appears in /config as Diff tool only while Claude Code is connected to a VS Code or JetBrains IDE.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented diffTool behavior.

name: disableAgentView
description: Turn off background agents and agent view: claude agents, --bg, /background, and the on-demand supervisor. Set it in managed settings to enforce it for an organization.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableAgentView behavior.

name: disableAllHooks
description: Turn off hooks, any custom status line, and any custom file suggestion command. Use it to turn all of these off temporarily without deleting them from your settings.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableAllHooks behavior.

name: disableArtifact
description: Deprecated, and replaced by enableArtifact. Claude Code still honors disableArtifact: true as equivalent to enableArtifact: false, and ignores disableArtifact: false.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableArtifact behavior.
when_not_to_use: Avoid this deprecated setting in new configuration; use the documented replacement when available.

name: disableAutoMode
description: Remove auto mode from the Shift+Tab cycle. Any session that would otherwise start in auto mode, whether from --permission-mode auto, a settings file, or the built-in default, starts in default instead. Administrators set it in managed settings to prevent developers in their organization from using auto mode.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableAutoMode behavior.

name: disableBrowserExternalNavigation
description: Turn off external browsing in the desktop app's Browser pane for people and Claude alike. Localhost dev server previews keep working. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.
syntax: disableBrowserExternalNavigation: <Boolean; only the JSON Boolean true takes effect>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableBrowserExternalNavigation behavior.

name: disableBundledSkills
description: Turn off the skills and workflows included with Claude Code. Claude Code removes bundled skills and workflows entirely, while built-in commands such as /init stay typable but are hidden from the model.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableBundledSkills behavior.

name: disableClaudeAiConnectors
description: Turn off the claude.ai MCP connectors Claude Code fetches itself, so it neither fetches nor connects them. A true in any settings file applies: a checked-in project .claude/settings.json can opt a repository out of those connectors, but a project-level false can't override a user- or managed-level true. Requires Claude Code v2.1.182 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableClaudeAiConnectors behavior.

conditions: Turn off the claude.ai MCP connectors Claude Code fetches itself, so it neither fetches nor connects them. A true in any settings file applies: a checked-in project .claude/settings.json can opt a repository out of those connectors, but a project-level false can't override a user- or managed-level true. Requires Claude Code v2.1.182 or later.

name: disableCommandPluginSources
description: Block the command plugin source, which installs a plugin by running a marketplace-declared command on the user's machine. When you set it to true, Claude Code never runs the command, doesn't install or update command-sourced plugins, and stops loading the ones already installed. Set it to false to allow them explicitly. Whenever it blocks command sources, whether you set it to true or leave it unset under allowManagedHooksOnly, it also blocks marketplace headersHelper commands, except for a marketplace that managed settings themselves declare. Requires Claude Code v2.1.229 or later, and the headersHelper block requires v2.1.238 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableCommandPluginSources behavior.

conditions: Block the command plugin source, which installs a plugin by running a marketplace-declared command on the user's machine. When you set it to true, Claude Code never runs the command, doesn't install or update command-sourced plugins, and stops loading the ones already installed. Set it to false to allow them explicitly. Whenever it blocks command sources, whether you set it to true or leave it unset under allowManagedHooksOnly, it also blocks marketplace headersHelper commands, except for a marketplace that managed settings themselves declare. Requires Claude Code v2.1.229 or later, and the headersHelper block requires v2.1.238 or later.

name: disableDeepLinkRegistration
description: Stop Claude Code from registering the claude-cli:// protocol handler with the operating system, which it otherwise does after you send the first prompt of an interactive session. Deep links let external tools open a Claude Code session with a pre-filled prompt. Set this in environments where protocol handler registration is restricted or managed separately.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableDeepLinkRegistration behavior.

name: disableDesktopLocalSessions
description: Turn off Code sessions that run on the device in the desktop app, for deployments where developers should work on remote machines over SSH. In the Code tab, the Local environment stays in the environment dropdown but is grayed out and can't be selected, with a tooltip saying your organization turned it off; on Windows the WSL entry is grayed out the same way, though whether WSL sessions run on a managed device at all is governed separately. New sessions default to the first SSH connection if one is configured, and the app refuses to start or resume a session on the device, including an SSH connection back to the same machine. SSH sessions to other hosts and cloud sessions are unaffected. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.37937.0 or later.
syntax: disableDesktopLocalSessions: <Boolean; only the JSON Boolean true takes effect>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableDesktopLocalSessions behavior.

conditions: Turn off Code sessions that run on the device in the desktop app, for deployments where developers should work on remote machines over SSH. In the Code tab, the Local environment stays in the environment dropdown but is grayed out and can't be selected, with a tooltip saying your organization turned it off; on Windows the WSL entry is grayed out the same way, though whether WSL sessions run on a managed device at all is governed separately. New sessions default to the first SSH connection if one is configured, and the app refuses to start or resume a session on the device, including an SSH connection back to the same machine. SSH sessions to other hosts and cloud sessions are unaffected. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.37937.0 or later.

name: disableMobileSimulatorTools
description: Block Claude's tools for the desktop app's iOS Simulator pane. People keep manual use of the pane; only Claude's access is removed, and nobody can turn it back on from inside the app. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.
syntax: disableMobileSimulatorTools: <Boolean; only the JSON Boolean true takes effect>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableMobileSimulatorTools behavior.

name: disableRemoteControl
description: Turn off Remote Control: Claude Code then refuses claude remote-control, the --remote-control flag, auto-start, and the in-session toggle, and reports that your organization's policy disabled it. Place it in managed settings for per-device MDM enforcement.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableRemoteControl behavior.

name: disableSideloadFlags
description: Reject the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass strictKnownMarketplaces for a single run. Claude Code exits with an error naming the rejected flags, and applies the same check to surfaces that start the CLI with these flags internally, currently Cowork local sessions in the desktop app. In cloud sessions, Claude Code drops the MCP servers the server delivered through --mcp-config, other than in-process type: "sdk" entries, and starts the session. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableSideloadFlags behavior.

conditions: Reject the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass strictKnownMarketplaces for a single run. Claude Code exits with an error naming the rejected flags, and applies the same check to surfaces that start the CLI with these flags internally, currently Cowork local sessions in the desktop app. In cloud sessions, Claude Code drops the MCP servers the server delivered through --mcp-config, other than in-process type: "sdk" entries, and starts the session. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.

name: disableSkillShellExecution
description: Turn off inline shell execution for !... and ! blocks in skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or additional-directory sources. Claude Code replaces each command with [shell command execution disabled by policy] instead of running it.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableSkillShellExecution behavior.

name: disableWorkflows
description: Turn off dynamic workflows and the bundled workflow commands for everyone your settings reach, such as an organization through managed settings. To turn workflows on or off just for yourself, use enableWorkflows instead, which the Dynamic workflows toggle in /config writes to your user settings.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disableWorkflows behavior.

name: disabledMcpjsonServers
description: Reject specific servers defined in a project's .mcp.json file so Claude Code never connects them or asks you to approve them. A rejection in any settings file applies, including a project .claude/settings.json checked into the repository.
syntax: disabledMcpjsonServers: <array of strings, the server names as they appear in .mcp.json>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented disabledMcpjsonServers behavior.

name: editorMode
description: Choose the key binding mode for the input prompt.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented editorMode behavior.

name: effortLevel
description: Persist the default reasoning effort for new Claude Code sessions.

examples.explanation: Start supported models with high reasoning effort by default.

when_to_use: Use when a consistent reasoning effort is appropriate across sessions.
when_not_to_use: Use --effort for a task-specific override.

conditions: Supported levels depend on the selected model.

name: emojiCompletionEnabled
description: Show emoji suggestions when you type : plus a shortcode in the prompt input, and replace a completed shortcode such as :heart: with its emoji. Set it to false to turn off both.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented emojiCompletionEnabled behavior.

name: enableAllProjectMcpServers
description: Approve every MCP server defined in project .mcp.json files without a prompt. Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you choose to approve all servers in the approval dialog.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enableAllProjectMcpServers behavior.

name: enableArtifact
description: Turn off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the Artifacts row off in /config, Claude Code writes this key to your user settings, so you don't usually edit it by hand. Requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enableArtifact behavior.

conditions: Turn off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the Artifacts row off in /config, Claude Code writes this key to your user settings, so you don't usually edit it by hand. Requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later.

name: enableWorkflows
description: Turn dynamic workflows on or off for yourself when your plan's default isn't what you want. Appears in /config as Dynamic workflows, which writes this key to your user settings and removes it again when you toggle back to your plan's default. To turn workflows off for everyone from managed settings, use disableWorkflows instead.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enableWorkflows behavior.

name: enabledMcpjsonServers
description: Approve specific servers defined in project .mcp.json files so Claude Code connects them without asking. Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you approve a server in the approval dialog.
syntax: enabledMcpjsonServers: <array of strings, the server names as they appear in .mcp.json>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enabledMcpjsonServers behavior.

name: enabledPlugins
description: Turn individual plugins on or off, keyed by plugin-name@marketplace-name. A plugin with no entry at any scope falls back to its defaultEnabled value. When you enable or disable a plugin with /plugin or claude plugin enable, Claude Code writes this key for you.
syntax: enabledPlugins: <object mapping plugin-name@marketplace-name to a Boolean>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enabledPlugins behavior.

name: enforceAvailableModels
description: The /model picker has a Default option that resolves to your organization default model when one applies, and otherwise to your account type's default. An availableModels allowlist limits the models you can name, but on its own it leaves Default alone, so Default can still resolve to a model outside the list. This key closes that gap. Requires Claude Code v2.1.175 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented enforceAvailableModels behavior.

conditions: The /model picker has a Default option that resolves to your organization default model when one applies, and otherwise to your account type's default. An availableModels allowlist limits the models you can name, but on its own it leaves Default alone, so Default can still resolve to a model outside the list. This key closes that gap. Requires Claude Code v2.1.175 or later.

name: env
description: Set environment variables for every session and for the subprocesses Claude Code starts from it. Any variable in the environment variables reference can go here, which is how you apply one to every session or roll it out to your team.
syntax: env: <object mapping variable names to string values>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented env behavior.

name: externalEditorContext
description: When you press Ctrl+G, Claude Code opens the prompt you're typing in your external editor. With this key on, the editor buffer starts with Claude's previous response as # comment lines, so you can read it while you write, and Claude Code strips those lines when you save. Appears in /config as Show last response in external editor.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented externalEditorContext behavior.

name: extraKnownMarketplaces
description: Register additional plugin marketplaces by name, so that people who open the repository, or everyone your managed settings reach, get the marketplace without adding it themselves. Claude Code registers each marketplace it doesn't already know. Whether a plugin that enabledPlugins names from it installs depends on the plugin's source and which file enables it; that entry has the rules.
syntax: extraKnownMarketplaces: <object mapping a marketplace name to an object with a source object and an optional autoUpdate Boolean>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented extraKnownMarketplaces behavior.

name: fallbackModel
description: Name backup models for Claude Code to try, in order, when your primary model is overloaded or unavailable. Claude Code switches to the next available model in the chain for the rest of the turn and shows a notice. Without a chain, Claude Code retries the same model and then surfaces the server's error, and you retry or switch models yourself.
syntax: fallbackModel: <array of model aliases or IDs; "default" expands to the default model>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented fallbackModel behavior.

name: fastMode
description: Turn fast mode on for sessions where it's available, for interactive work like rapid iteration or live debugging where you want speed at a higher cost per token. You don't usually edit this key by hand: running /fast writes fastMode: true to ~/.claude/settings.json, and running it again to turn fast mode off removes the key. Fast mode runs only on Opus 5 and Opus 4.8: turning it on from another model switches you to Opus, and switching to an unsupported model turns it off. See Switch models while fast mode is on.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented fastMode behavior.

name: fastModePerSessionOptIn
description: Normally, running /fast saves fastMode to a person's user settings, so fast mode is on at the start of every later session. Set this key to true to stop that: a saved fastMode: true no longer turns fast mode on at session start, and each person has to run /fast in each session they want it. Claude Code leaves the fastMode key in their file, so turning this key off restores the old behavior. Owners on Team or Enterprise plans can deploy it organization-wide through server-managed settings.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented fastModePerSessionOptIn behavior.

conditions: Normally, running /fast saves fastMode to a person's user settings, so fast mode is on at the start of every later session. Set this key to true to stop that: a saved fastMode: true no longer turns fast mode on at session start, and each person has to run /fast in each session they want it. Claude Code leaves the fastMode key in their file, so turning this key off restores the old behavior. Owners on Team or Enterprise plans can deploy it organization-wide through server-managed settings.

name: feedbackDrafts
description: Control Claude-drafted feedback: whether Claude can queue feedback drafts for you to review, and whether Claude Code shows a card when Claude queues one.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented feedbackDrafts behavior.

name: feedbackSurveyRate
description: Set the probability that the session quality survey appears when a session is eligible for it. Set 0 to keep the survey from appearing.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented feedbackSurveyRate behavior.

name: fileCheckpointingEnabled
description: Have Claude Code snapshot files before each edit so /rewind can restore them. Appears in /config as Rewind code (checkpoints), and toggling it there writes this key to your user settings.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented fileCheckpointingEnabled behavior.

name: fileSuggestion
description: Run your own command to supply @ file path autocomplete instead of the built-in file suggestion. The built-in suggestion uses fast filesystem traversal; a large monorepo may do better with project-specific indexing such as a pre-built file index.
syntax: fileSuggestion: <object with type, always "command", and command, the shell command to run>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented fileSuggestion behavior.

name: footerLinksRegexes
description: Render extra clickable badges in the footer below the input box when a regex matches turn output: tool results, including file contents and fetched pages, and Claude's own responses. Use it to turn IDs printed by project CLIs, such as review tools and issue trackers, into session links. Requires Claude Code v2.1.176 or later.
syntax: footerLinksRegexes: <array of objects, each with type set to "regex", a pattern regex, a url template, and an optional label; {name} placeholders in url and label are filled from named capture groups in pattern>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented footerLinksRegexes behavior.

conditions: Render extra clickable badges in the footer below the input box when a regex matches turn output: tool results, including file contents and fetched pages, and Claude's own responses.
