Use it to turn IDs printed by project CLIs, such as review tools and issue trackers, into session links. Requires Claude Code v2.1.176 or later.

name: forceLoginGatewayUrl
description: Set the gateway URL the /login Cloud gateway screen connects to, so people reach your cloud gateway without typing its address. The screen has no URL field: with this key set, it shows your gateway URL and connects when the person presses Enter; without it, it tells them to contact their IT administrator. When forceLoginMethod is unset, this key alone opens the Cloud gateway screen. forceLoginMethod: "gateway" also opens it and removes the login-method picker, and a claudeai or console value there takes precedence over this key. Set both keys so the screen connects instead of showing an error.
syntax: forceLoginGatewayUrl: <string, a full URL including the scheme>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented forceLoginGatewayUrl behavior.

name: forceLoginMethod
description: Restrict which kind of account people can log in with. Set "claudeai" to allow only claude.ai accounts, "console" to allow only Claude Console accounts, or "gateway" to send people to a cloud gateway instead of a first-party login. Administrators set it in managed settings and pair it with forceLoginOrgUUID to keep developers' claude.ai logins inside one organization.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented forceLoginMethod behavior.

name: forceLoginOrgUUID
description: From a managed source, require claude.ai account logins to belong to one Anthropic organization, a single UUID, or to any of several, an array. From any settings file, a single UUID also pre-selects that organization during a claude.ai or Claude Console login; an array pre-selects nothing.
syntax: forceLoginOrgUUID: <string, one UUID, or array of strings, several UUIDs>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented forceLoginOrgUUID behavior.

name: forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
description: Block CLI startup until Claude Code has freshly fetched server-managed settings. If the fetch fails, Claude Code exits instead of continuing with cached or no settings. Set it when your environment can't accept even a brief window in which a session runs without its managed policy.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented forceRemoteSettingsRefresh behavior.

name: gcpAuthRefresh
description: Run your own command to refresh Google Cloud Application Default Credentials when Claude Code finds they've expired or can't be loaded, so Google Cloud's Agent Platform requests keep working without you re-authenticating by hand.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented gcpAuthRefresh behavior.

name: hooks
description: Run your own commands, prompts, agents, HTTP requests, or MCP tools as hooks at points in Claude Code's lifecycle, such as before a tool call or when a session starts; the hooks reference lists every event, its payload, and its exit codes. Each event maps to a list of matcher groups, and each group lists the handlers to run when the matcher applies.
syntax: hooks: <object keyed by hook event; each value is an array of { "matcher", "hooks" } groups whose hooks entries have a type of "command", "prompt", "agent", "http", or "mcp_tool">
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented hooks behavior.

name: httpHookAllowedEnvVars
description: An HTTP hook can put the value of an environment variable into a request header, for example an Authorization: Bearer $HOOK_TOKEN header, but only for variables the hook lists in its own allowedEnvVars. This key sets an outer limit on that list for every HTTP hook: a hook can use a variable only if both its own allowedEnvVars and this key name it. Use it to stop a hook from reading a secret it shouldn't, even when the hook's definition asks for it.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented httpHookAllowedEnvVars behavior.

name: includeCoAuthoredBy
description: Deprecated since v2.0.62, when attribution replaced it. Claude Code still reads it, but new configurations should set attribution.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented includeCoAuthoredBy behavior.
when_not_to_use: Avoid this deprecated setting in new configuration; use the documented replacement when available.

name: includeGitInstructions
description: At session start, Claude Code adds two git-related pieces to Claude's prompt: its built-in instructions for how to write commits and pull requests, in the Bash tool's description, and a git status snapshot of your repository in the system prompt, meaning the current branch, the main branch, git status output, and recent commits. Set this key to false to leave both out, for example when you use your own git workflow skills.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented includeGitInstructions behavior.

name: inputNeededNotifEnabled
description: Get a push notification on your phone when a permission prompt or question is waiting for your input. Claude Code sends these only while Remote Control is connected. Appears in /config as Push when actions required.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented inputNeededNotifEnabled behavior.

name: isolatePeerMachines
description: Require your explicit approval before Claude's SendMessage reaches one of your sessions beyond this machine; see Require approval for cross-machine messages. The approval prompt appears even in bypassPermissions mode.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented isolatePeerMachines behavior.

name: keybindingFlavor
description: Choose which convention Ctrl+W follows in the prompt input. Set it to "readline" to make Ctrl+W delete back to the previous whitespace, as Bash does, so a path or a --flag=value goes in one press. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented keybindingFlavor behavior.

conditions: Choose which convention Ctrl+W follows in the prompt input. Set it to "readline" to make Ctrl+W delete back to the previous whitespace, as Bash does, so a path or a --flag=value goes in one press. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later.

name: language
description: Have Claude respond in a language other than English by default. There is no fixed list for responses: Claude Code adds the value verbatim to the system prompt as an instruction to always respond in that language, so any language name Claude can read works. Claude Code doesn't check the value, so a misspelled name reaches Claude as written rather than producing an error. The same value sets the language for voice dictation, which does have a fixed list of supported dictation languages, and for auto-generated session titles.
syntax: language: <string, any language name, such as "japanese", "spanish", or "french"; Claude Code doesn't validate it>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented language behavior.

name: managedSourcesBehavior
description: Choose whether Claude Code applies only the highest-priority managed source your organization delivers, or combines every admin source it delivers. By default Claude Code takes the highest-priority source that carries a policy key and ignores the rest. A policy key is any settings key other than this one and wslInheritsWindowsSettings. So once server-managed settings or an MDM policy deliver a policy key, a managed-settings.json file contributes only the keys Claude Code reads from every admin source. With "merge", every admin source you deliver contributes its keys to one combined policy. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented managedSourcesBehavior behavior.

conditions: Choose whether Claude Code applies only the highest-priority managed source your organization delivers, or combines every admin source it delivers. By default Claude Code takes the highest-priority source that carries a policy key and ignores the rest. A policy key is any settings key other than this one and wslInheritsWindowsSettings. So once server-managed settings or an MDM policy deliver a policy key, a managed-settings.json file contributes only the keys Claude Code reads from every admin source. With "merge", every admin source you deliver contributes its keys to one combined policy. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

name: minimumVersion
description: Keep background auto-updates and claude update from installing any version below this one, so moving to the "stable" channel doesn't downgrade you from a newer "latest" build. Claude Code writes this key for you when you choose to stay on your current version while switching channels in /config, and clears it when you switch back to "latest".
syntax: minimumVersion: <string, a version number such as "2.1.100">
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented minimumVersion behavior.

name: model
description: Set the model Claude Code starts with for new sessions unless a higher-precedence per-session override is supplied.

examples.explanation: Use the current Sonnet alias for new sessions by default.

when_to_use: Use when most new sessions should start with one model or alias.
when_not_to_use: Use --model for a one-session override.

conditions: Managed availableModels policy can restrict selection.

name: modelOverrides
description: Map Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific model IDs, such as Amazon Bedrock inference profile ARNs. Each model picker entry then uses its mapped value when calling the provider API. Administrators use this on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry to route each model version to a specific inference profile, version name, or deployment for governance, cost allocation, or regional routing.
syntax: modelOverrides: <object mapping model ID to provider model ID>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented modelOverrides behavior.

name: modelPicker
description: List the models the /model picker offers, in the order you write them and under labels you choose, so the picker lists the models your organization runs, after the built-in lineup or instead of it. Each row's model is taken verbatim, so it accepts anything --model accepts: an alias such as opus, an Anthropic model ID, or a provider-format ID for Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or an LLM gateway. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
syntax: modelPicker: <object with an options array of rows and an optional replaceBuiltInOptions Boolean>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented modelPicker behavior.

conditions: List the models the /model picker offers, in the order you write them and under labels you choose, so the picker lists the models your organization runs, after the built-in lineup or instead of it. Each row's model is taken verbatim, so it accepts anything --model accepts: an alias such as opus, an Anthropic model ID, or a provider-format ID for Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or an LLM gateway. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

name: modelPricing
description: Report spend at the rates your organization pays instead of list price. Set it when your organization has contracted rates, so the dollar figures developers see match your bill. Claude Code applies the rates in /usage, the status line, the Agent SDK's total_cost_usd, the --max-budget-usd limit, and the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events. You supply the rates: Claude Code doesn't read them from your contract or the Claude Console. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
syntax: modelPricing: <object with an optional multiplier and an optional overrides map>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented modelPricing behavior.

conditions: Report spend at the rates your organization pays instead of list price. Set it when your organization has contracted rates, so the dollar figures developers see match your bill. Claude Code applies the rates in /usage, the status line, the Agent SDK's total_cost_usd, the --max-budget-usd limit, and the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events. You supply the rates: Claude Code doesn't read them from your contract or the Claude Console. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

name: otelHeadersHelper
description: Run your own command to generate the headers Claude Code sends with OpenTelemetry exports, for backends whose tokens rotate. Claude Code runs it at startup and periodically after that, and expects a JSON object of string header values on stdout.
syntax: otelHeadersHelper: <string, an executable path or a shell command line>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented otelHeadersHelper behavior.

name: outputStyle
description: Select an output style by name. An output style is a saved set of instructions that Claude Code adds to the system prompt to change Claude's role, tone, and output format, such as the built-in Explanatory and Learning styles or one you wrote yourself.
syntax: outputStyle: <string, the name of a built-in or custom output style>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented outputStyle behavior.

name: parentSettingsBehavior
description: Choose whether Claude Code applies managed settings supplied by an embedding host process, such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension, when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present. With "first-wins", Claude Code drops the host-supplied settings; with "merge", it applies them under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. Set "merge" when a host needs to pass its own restrictions to the sessions it launches, for example Claude Desktop delivering a gateway's egress allowlist.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented parentSettingsBehavior behavior.

name: permissionExplainerEnabled
description: When Claude asks permission to run a Bash or PowerShell command, you can press Ctrl+E on the prompt to get a model-generated explanation of the command: what it does, why Claude is running it, and what could go wrong, labeled Low risk, Med risk, or High risk. Claude Code asks the model for the explanation only when you press the shortcut, and showing it doesn't run the command. Set this key to false to turn the shortcut off.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissionExplainerEnabled behavior.

name: permissions
description: Control which tools Claude can use without asking, which ones always prompt, and which ones are blocked, and set the permission mode a session starts in. Every permissions.* key below nests under this object.
syntax: permissions: <object with allow, ask, deny, additionalDirectories, defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode, and disableAutoMode>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions behavior.

name: permissions.additionalDirectories
description: Give Claude file access to directories outside the one you started in, as additional working directories. Most .claude/ configuration is not discovered from these directories.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.additionalDirectories behavior.

name: permissions.allow
description: List the tool uses Claude Code approves without asking you. In an MCP rule, * can appear only in the tool name after the mcp____ prefix, such as mcp__github__get_*; it can't appear in the server name.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.allow behavior.

name: permissions.ask
description: List the tool uses that prompt you for confirmation even in a permission mode that would otherwise approve them, such as acceptEdits or bypassPermissions. In dontAsk mode Claude Code denies a matching tool use instead of prompting.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.ask behavior.

name: permissions.defaultMode
description: Set the permission mode used when new Claude Code sessions start.

examples.explanation: Start new sessions in read-only plan mode by default.

when_to_use: Use to establish a safer or workflow-specific starting mode across sessions.
when_not_to_use: Use --permission-mode when only one invocation should differ.

conditions: Managed settings can override this value.

name: permissions.deny
description: List the tool uses Claude Code blocks. Use it for files that hold API keys, secrets, or environment values: Claude Code excludes matching files from file discovery and search results, denies reads of them, and blocks the Edit and Write tools on the matching paths. Read and Edit deny rules apply to Claude's built-in file tools and to file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash, such as cat, head, tail, and sed; they don't apply to arbitrary subprocesses, so for OS-level enforcement enable the sandbox.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.deny behavior.

name: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
description: Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode. Claude Code then rejects the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag, and ignores an agent definition's permissionMode: bypassPermissions, so the subagent runs with the parent session's permission mode.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode behavior.

name: plansDirectory
description: Choose where Claude Code stores the plan files it writes in plan mode. Claude Code resolves the path relative to the project root and keeps the default when the path resolves outside it.
syntax: plansDirectory: <string, a path relative to the project root>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented plansDirectory behavior.

name: pluginConfigs
description: Store the non-sensitive answers you give a plugin's userConfig configuration dialog, keyed by plugin ID. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you fill in the dialog, so you don't need to edit it by hand. Sensitive options go to the macOS Keychain instead, or to ~/.claude/.credentials.json on platforms without a supported keychain.
syntax: pluginConfigs: <object mapping a plugin ID to an object with an options field, mapping each option name to a string, number, Boolean, or array of strings, and an optional mcpServers field holding per-server user configuration values in the same shape>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented pluginConfigs behavior.

name: pluginSuggestionMarketplaces
description: Name the marketplaces whose plugins can appear as contextual install suggestions, in spinner tips and pinned at the top of the /plugin Discover tab. The built-in first-party frontend-design tip is unaffected. Suggestions come from each plugin's relevance declaration in its marketplace entry.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented pluginSuggestionMarketplaces behavior.

name: pluginTrustMessage
description: Add your organization's own text to the plugin trust warning Claude Code shows before installation, for example to confirm that plugins from your internal marketplace are vetted.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented pluginTrustMessage behavior.

name: policyHelper
description: Run an executable you deploy that computes managed settings at startup, so you can derive policy from device posture, identity, or a remote service instead of a static file. Claude Code runs the helper before it accepts the first prompt and treats the settings it emits as the managed settings for the session.
syntax: policyHelper: <object with path, timeoutMs, and refreshIntervalMs>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented policyHelper behavior.

name: policyHelper.path
description: Name the helper executable Claude Code runs. Claude Code refuses to start when the path isn't absolute, or on Windows when it doesn't end in .exe.
syntax: policyHelper.path: <string, an absolute path in normalized form, without . or .. segments>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented policyHelper.path behavior.

name: policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs
description: Have Claude Code re-run the helper in the background on an interval so policy changes reach a running session. When a refresh succeeds, its output replaces the previous managed settings without a restart; when a refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the policy it already has.
syntax: policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs: <integer, milliseconds: 0 to disable refresh, otherwise at least 60000>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs behavior.

name: policyHelper.timeoutMs
description: Set how long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented policyHelper.timeoutMs behavior.

name: prUrlTemplate
description: Point the PR links Claude Code renders, in the footer badge and in tool-result summaries, at an internal code-review tool instead of github.com. Claude Code substitutes {host}, {owner}, {repo}, {number}, and {url} from the gh-reported PR URL. The GitLab merge request badge keeps its GitLab URL.
syntax: prUrlTemplate: <string, a URL template using any of the five placeholders>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented prUrlTemplate behavior.

name: preferredNotifChannel
description: Choose how Claude Code notifies you when a task completes or a permission prompt is waiting. Appears in /config as Local notifications.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented preferredNotifChannel behavior.

name: prefersReducedMotion
description: Reduce or turn off interface animations such as the spinner, shimmer, and flash effects. Appears in /config as Reduce motion.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented prefersReducedMotion behavior.

name: processWrapper
description: On macOS and Linux, place a corporate launcher command in front of the background processes Claude Code starts. Claude Code runs the launcher with its own command line appended, so the launcher must exec into Claude Code; see Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher for the launcher contract. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later.
syntax: processWrapper: <string, the launcher command as an argv prefix, such as an absolute path with optional arguments>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented processWrapper behavior.

conditions: On macOS and Linux, place a corporate launcher command in front of the background processes Claude Code starts. Claude Code runs the launcher with its own command line appended, so the launcher must exec into Claude Code; see Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher for the launcher contract. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later.

name: promptCacheTtl
description: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the main conversation. This key applies to your interactive, -p, and Agent SDK turns, together with the helpers Claude Code runs inline with them. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented promptCacheTtl behavior.

conditions: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the main conversation. This key applies to your interactive, -p, and Agent SDK turns, together with the helpers Claude Code runs inline with them. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

name: promptSuggestionEnabled
description: Show or hide prompt suggestions, the grayed-out predictions that appear in your prompt input. Set it to false, or turn off Prompt suggestions in /config, to hide them.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented promptSuggestionEnabled behavior.

name: remote.defaultEnvironmentId
description: Pick the default cloud environment for cloud sessions you create from the CLI, such as with claude --cloud. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you pick an environment with /remote-env.
syntax: remote.defaultEnvironmentId: <string, an environment ID such as env_... or ccpool_...>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented remote.defaultEnvironmentId behavior.

name: remoteControlAtStartup
description: Connect Remote Control automatically when each interactive session starts, instead of waiting for /remote-control. Set it to true to turn auto-connect on, false to turn it off. Appears in /config as Enable Remote Control for all sessions.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented remoteControlAtStartup behavior.

name: requiredMaximumVersion
description: Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization's approved method; claude install may also work. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.
syntax: requiredMaximumVersion: <string, a version number such as "2.1.150"; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented requiredMaximumVersion behavior.

conditions: Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization's approved method; claude install may also work. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.

name: requiredMinimumVersion
description: Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization's approved method. The check runs at startup only, so a session that's already running continues. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.
syntax: requiredMinimumVersion: <string, a version number such as "2.1.150"; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented requiredMinimumVersion behavior.

conditions: Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization's approved method. The check runs at startup only, so a session that's already running continues. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.

name: respectGitignore
description: Control whether the @ file picker leaves out files that match .gitignore patterns. Appears in /config as Respect .gitignore in file picker.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented respectGitignore behavior.

name: respondToBashCommands
description: Choose whether Claude responds after you run a shell command with the ! prefix in the input box. By default, Claude Code adds the command's output to the conversation and Claude replies to it. Set this key to false to add the output to context without a reply, so you can run several commands and ask about them together. Requires Claude Code v2.1.186 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented respondToBashCommands behavior.

conditions: Choose whether Claude responds after you run a shell command with the ! prefix in the input box. By default, Claude Code adds the command's output to the conversation and Claude replies to it. Set this key to false to add the output to context without a reply, so you can run several commands and ask about them together. Requires Claude Code v2.1.186 or later.

name: sandbox
description: Isolate the Bash commands Claude runs from your filesystem and network with sandboxing. Turn the sandbox on with enabled, then narrow or widen what sandboxed commands can touch with the filesystem, network, and credentials sub-objects. The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.
syntax: sandbox: <object with enabled, failIfUnavailable, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, excludedCommands, allowUnsandboxedCommands, enableWeakerNestedSandbox, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation, allowAppleEvents, bwrapPath, socatPath, ignoreViolations, and ripgrep, plus the filesystem, network, and credentials objects>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox behavior.

name: sandbox.allowAppleEvents
description: Let sandboxed commands on macOS send Apple Events, which open, osascript, and tools that open URLs in a browser need; without it they fail with error -600. This removes code-execution isolation: sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can send AppleScript commands to running applications such as Terminal, subject to the per-app macOS automation-consent prompt (TCC).
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.allowAppleEvents behavior.

name: sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands
description: Let Claude retry a command outside the sandbox with the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter after the sandbox blocks it. Set it to false so Claude Code ignores that parameter completely and every command must run sandboxed or appear in excludedCommands, which the /sandbox Overrides tab shows as Strict sandbox mode. Use false in managed settings for policies that require strict sandboxing.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands behavior.

name: sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed
description: Let Claude Code run sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt. Commands that can't run in the sandbox still go through the regular permission flow, and deny rules and content-scoped ask rules such as Bash(git push *) still apply; a bare Bash ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands. Set it to false to send sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow too, which the /sandbox Mode tab calls regular permissions mode.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed behavior.

name: sandbox.bwrapPath
description: Point the sandbox at a bubblewrap binary installed outside PATH, such as a vendored copy on an air-gapped host. Claude Code uses the path both for the startup dependency check and when it wraps each sandboxed command.
syntax: sandbox.bwrapPath: <string, an absolute path; Claude Code drops a relative path and falls back to PATH lookup>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.bwrapPath behavior.

name: sandbox.credentials
description: Declare the credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands. Each entry names a file path or a variable name and a mode: deny hides the credential inside the sandbox, and mask shows sandboxed commands a placeholder while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests. Claude Code protects only the entries you list; there is no built-in credential deny list. Requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later.
syntax: sandbox.credentials: <object with files, envVars, allowPlaintextInject, awsPairs, and sigv4>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.credentials behavior.

conditions: Declare the credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands. Each entry names a file path or a variable name and a mode: deny hides the credential inside the sandbox, and mask shows sandboxed commands a placeholder while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests. Claude Code protects only the entries you list; there is no built-in credential deny list. Requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later.

name: sandbox.credentials.allowPlaintextInject
description: Allow mask substitution on plain HTTP requests as well as TLS-terminated HTTPS. On plain HTTP the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext, so leave this off outside trusted test networks. Requires Claude Code v2.1.199 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.credentials.allowPlaintextInject behavior.

conditions: Allow mask substitution on plain HTTP requests as well as TLS-terminated HTTPS. On plain HTTP the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext, so leave this off outside trusted test networks. Requires Claude Code v2.1.199 or later.

name: sandbox.credentials.awsPairs
description: Group masked environment variables that form one AWS credential for SigV4 re-signing when your credential lives in variables with non-standard names. Claude Code links the conventional AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN trio automatically when you mask their whole values, so you need this key only for other names. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
syntax: sandbox.credentials.awsPairs: <array of objects, each with accessKeyIdVar, secretAccessKeyVar, and optionally sessionTokenVar, naming sandbox.credentials.envVars entries>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.credentials.awsPairs behavior.

conditions: Group masked environment variables that form one AWS credential for SigV4 re-signing when your credential lives in variables with non-standard names. Claude Code links the conventional AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN trio automatically when you mask their whole values, so you need this key only for other names. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

name: sandbox.credentials.envVars
description: Protect environment variables from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code removes the variable from the environment of sandboxed commands. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands see a per-session sentinel value, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts, so tools such as gh and npm keep authenticating without ever holding the real credential. Requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later, and "mode": "mask" requires v2.1.199 or later.
syntax: sandbox.credentials.envVars: <array of objects, each with name and a mode of "deny" or "mask", plus the optional mask fields for environment variables>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.credentials.envVars behavior.

conditions: Protect environment variables from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code removes the variable from the environment of sandboxed commands. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands see a per-session sentinel value, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts, so tools such as gh and npm keep authenticating without ever holding the real credential. Requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later, and "mode": "mask" requires v2.1.199 or later.

name: sandbox.credentials.files
description: Protect credential files or directories from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code blocks reads of the path inside the sandbox, the same read block as sandbox.filesystem.denyRead. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands on Linux and WSL2 read a sentinel copy of the file, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts; on macOS the file is unreadable inside the sandbox instead. Requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later, and "mode": "mask" requires v2.1.221 or later.
syntax: sandbox.credentials.files: <array of objects, each with path and a mode of "deny" or "mask", plus the optional mask fields for files>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.credentials.files behavior.

conditions: Protect credential files or directories from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code blocks reads of the path inside the sandbox, the same read block as sandbox.filesystem.denyRead. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands on Linux and WSL2 read a sentinel copy of the file, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts; on macOS the file is unreadable inside the sandbox instead. Requires Claude Code v2.1.187 or later, and "mode": "mask" requires v2.1.221 or later.

name: sandbox.credentials.sigv4
description: Choose what the sandbox proxy does with AWS request forms it can't re-sign: streaming for aws-chunked streaming uploads, presigned for presigned URLs, and sigv4a for SigV4A asymmetric signatures. This applies only to requests signed with a masked pair's placeholder access key ID. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
syntax: sandbox.credentials.sigv4: <object with streaming, presigned, and sigv4a, each one of:>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.credentials.sigv4 behavior.

conditions: Choose what the sandbox proxy does with AWS request forms it can't re-sign: streaming for aws-chunked streaming uploads, presigned for presigned URLs, and sigv4a for SigV4A asymmetric signatures. This applies only to requests signed with a masked pair's placeholder access key ID. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

name: sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox
description: Run the Linux sandbox inside an unprivileged Docker container, where bubblewrap can't mount a fresh /proc. Instead the inner sandbox bind-mounts the container's existing /proc, which exposes process information that a fresh mount would hide. This reduces security; use it only when the outer container already provides the isolation you need.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox behavior.

name: sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation
description: Let sandboxed commands on macOS reach the system TLS trust service, com.apple.trustd.agent. Go-based tools such as gh, gcloud, and terraform need it to verify TLS certificates when you use network.httpProxyPort with a MITM proxy and a custom CA. This reduces security by opening a potential data exfiltration path through the trust service.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation behavior.

name: sandbox.enabled
description: Turn on sandboxing for Bash commands. When you pick a mode in the /sandbox panel, Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json for the current project; set it in ~/.claude/settings.json to sandbox every project.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.enabled behavior.

name: sandbox.excludedCommands
description: Name commands that Claude Code always runs outside the sandbox, such as tools that don't work under it. Each entry uses the same syntax as the content of a Bash(...) permission rule: an exact command, a prefix such as docker *, or a wildcard pattern. When any part of a compound command matches an entry, Claude Code runs the whole command unsandboxed.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.excludedCommands behavior.

name: sandbox.failIfUnavailable
description: Make Claude Code exit with an error at startup when sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox can't start, because a dependency is missing or the platform is unsupported. Without it, Claude Code shows a warning and runs commands unsandboxed. Use it in managed settings when your organization requires sandboxing as a hard gate.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.failIfUnavailable behavior.

conditions: Make Claude Code exit with an error at startup when sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox can't start, because a dependency is missing or the platform is unsupported. Without it, Claude Code shows a warning and runs commands unsandboxed. Use it in managed settings when your organization requires sandboxing as a hard gate.

name: sandbox.filesystem
description: Control which paths sandboxed commands can read and write. By default they can write to the working directory, any directories you add with --add-dir, and the session temp directory, and can read the rest of the filesystem, including credential files. Widen or narrow that with the four path lists, or switch the filesystem layer off with disabled. See Filesystem isolation for the default boundaries.
syntax: sandbox.filesystem: <object with allowWrite, denyWrite, denyRead, and allowRead arrays, plus the allowManagedReadPathsOnly and disabled Booleans>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem behavior.

name: sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly
description: Honor only the allowRead entries that come from managed settings, so developers can't re-open read access to paths your organization blocked. Claude Code still merges denyRead entries from every settings file the session loads.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly behavior.

name: sandbox.filesystem.allowRead
description: Re-open reading for specific paths inside a region that denyRead blocks, to build workspace-only read access. An exact or wildcard denyRead entry stays blocked inside a broader allowRead, as the overlap table shows. When a wildcard denyRead entry such as ~//.env matches a directory, Claude Code blocks reads of its contents as well. Before v2.1.236 on macOS, Claude Code re-opened the paths a wildcard denyRead entry matched wherever a broader allowRead entry covered them, and left a matched directory's contents readable.
syntax: sandbox.filesystem.allowRead: <array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem.allowRead behavior.

name: sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite
description: Add paths where sandboxed commands can write, beyond the working directory, the directories you've added with --add-dir or /add-dir, and the session temp directory. Use it when a subprocess such as kubectl or a build tool needs to write outside the project.
syntax: sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite: <array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite behavior.

name: sandbox.filesystem.denyRead
description: Block sandboxed commands from reading specific paths, such as credential files that the default read policy would otherwise expose. To protect a credential file and keep it usable through the sandbox proxy, see sandbox.credentials instead.
syntax: sandbox.filesystem.denyRead: <array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem.denyRead behavior.

name: sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite
description: Block sandboxed commands from writing to specific paths, including paths inside a directory that is otherwise writable.
syntax: sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite: <array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite behavior.

name: sandbox.filesystem.disabled
description: Skip filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read and write access to the host filesystem, and their network egress stays confined to network.allowedDomains. Use it when you sandbox to control where commands connect rather than what they write. Requires Claude Code v2.1.216 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.filesystem.disabled behavior.

conditions: Skip filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read and write access to the host filesystem, and their network egress stays confined to network.allowedDomains. Use it when you sandbox to control where commands connect rather than what they write. Requires Claude Code v2.1.216 or later.

name: sandbox.ignoreViolations
description: Silence sandbox violation reports for paths you expect a command to probe and be refused, such as a tool that checks /etc/hosts on startup, so those denials don't show up as violations or in what Claude sees. The sandbox still blocks the access; only the report is suppressed. Keys are substrings to match against the command, with * matching every command, and values are substrings of the violation to ignore for that command, such as a filesystem path.
syntax: sandbox.ignoreViolations: <object mapping a command substring to an array of violation substrings, usually paths>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.ignoreViolations behavior.

name: sandbox.network
description: Control which hosts, ports, and sockets sandboxed commands can reach. The sandbox routes outbound traffic through a proxy that enforces these lists; see Network isolation for how the proxy decides and when it prompts.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network behavior.

name: sandbox.network.allowAllUnixSockets
description: Let sandboxed commands connect to every Unix socket. On Linux and WSL2, the sandbox's seccomp filter blocks socket(AF_UNIX, ...) calls, so this is the only way to permit Unix sockets there. When the filter is missing, which /sandbox reports on its Dependencies tab, the sandbox doesn't block Unix-socket calls. See Set up Linux and WSL2 for where the filter comes from.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.allowAllUnixSockets behavior.

name: sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding
description: Let sandboxed commands bind to localhost ports on macOS, for example to start a dev server.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding behavior.

name: sandbox.network.allowMachLookup
description: List additional XPC and Mach service names the macOS sandbox may look up. Tools that communicate over XPC, such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright, need their services listed here.
syntax: sandbox.network.allowMachLookup: <array of strings, each a service name; a single trailing * matches a prefix, and "*" alone matches every service>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.allowMachLookup behavior.

name: sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly
description: Lock the network allowlist to what managed settings define. Claude Code then honors only allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules from managed settings, ignores domains from user, project, local, and --settings settings, and blocks a non-allowed domain automatically instead of prompting.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly behavior.

name: sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets
description: List the Unix socket paths sandboxed commands can connect to on macOS. Claude Code ignores this list on Linux and WSL2, where the seccomp filter can't inspect socket paths; use allowAllUnixSockets there instead.
syntax: sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets: <array of strings, each a socket path>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets behavior.

name: sandbox.network.allowedDomains
description: Pre-allow domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, so the sandbox doesn't prompt for them. Wildcards such as *.example.com match subdomains, and an optional :port suffix limits an entry to one port; an entry without a port matches every port.
syntax: sandbox.network.allowedDomains: <array of strings, each a domain, wildcard pattern, or IP literal, with an optional :port suffix>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.allowedDomains behavior.

name: sandbox.network.deniedDomains
description: Block domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, using the same wildcard, port, and IPv6 syntax as allowedDomains. A denied domain stays blocked even when an allowedDomains entry matches it too.
syntax: sandbox.network.deniedDomains: <array of strings, each a domain, wildcard pattern, or IP literal, with an optional :port suffix>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.deniedDomains behavior.

name: sandbox.network.httpProxyPort
description: Point the sandbox at your own HTTP proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Organizations do this to inspect HTTPS traffic, apply their own filtering rules, or log every request. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for HTTP traffic.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.httpProxyPort behavior.

name: sandbox.network.socksProxyPort
description: Point the sandbox at your own SOCKS5 proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for SOCKS traffic.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.socksProxyPort behavior.

name: sandbox.network.strictAllowlist
description: Deny sandboxed commands access to hosts outside the allowlist instead of prompting for approval. The allowlist is allowedDomains plus domains from WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules, or only the managed settings entries when allowManagedDomainsOnly is set. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.strictAllowlist behavior.

conditions: Deny sandboxed commands access to hosts outside the allowlist instead of prompting for approval. The allowlist is allowedDomains plus domains from WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules, or only the managed settings entries when allowManagedDomainsOnly is set. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

name: sandbox.network.tlsTerminate
description: Make the sandbox proxy terminate TLS so it can read the contents of HTTPS requests. This is experimental, and mask credential substitution requires it. Set {} to generate an ephemeral certificate authority for the session, or set caCertPath and caKeyPath to use your own.
syntax: sandbox.network.tlsTerminate: <object with optional caCertPath and caKeyPath strings, each a file path>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.network.tlsTerminate behavior.

name: sandbox.ripgrep
description: Point the sandbox at a ripgrep binary of your own instead of the one Claude Code uses, for example when your platform needs a differently built rg.
syntax: sandbox.ripgrep: <object with command, the path to the ripgrep binary, and optional args, an array of arguments to prepend>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.ripgrep behavior.

name: sandbox.socatPath
description: Point the sandbox network proxy at a socat binary installed outside PATH.
syntax: sandbox.socatPath: <string, an absolute path; Claude Code drops a relative path and falls back to PATH lookup>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sandbox.socatPath behavior.

name: showClearContextOnPlanAccept
description: When Claude finishes a plan in plan mode, it shows an approval menu. Planning can use a lot of context, so this key adds a first option to that menu, Yes, clear context and …, that approves the plan, clears the conversation context, and starts implementing from the plan alone. The rest of the label names the permission mode the session continues in, and shows how much of your context the planning used.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented showClearContextOnPlanAccept behavior.

name: showThinkingSummaries
description: See summaries of Claude's extended thinking in interactive sessions. Set it if you want the full summaries when you expand thinking with Ctrl+O. When unset or false, the Anthropic API redacts thinking blocks and Claude Code shows a collapsed stub; third-party providers don't redact.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented showThinkingSummaries behavior.

name: showTurnDuration
description: Show or hide the turn duration message after each response, such as "Cooked for 1m 6s". Appears in /config as Show turn duration.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented showTurnDuration behavior.

name: skillListingBudgetFraction
description: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills with their descriptions, and Claude Code caps that listing at a share of the context window. When the listing is over the cap, Claude Code keeps every skill's name but drops the descriptions of the least-used skills, so Claude can still invoke those skills but is less likely to choose one on its own. Raise this key to keep more descriptions visible at the cost of more context per turn.
syntax: skillListingBudgetFraction: <number, a fraction greater than 0 and at most 1>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented skillListingBudgetFraction behavior.

name: skillListingMaxDescChars
description: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills that shows each skill's description and when_to_use text. This key caps how many characters of that text Claude Code shows per skill; longer text is cut at the cap.
syntax: skillListingMaxDescChars: <number of characters, a positive integer>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented skillListingMaxDescChars behavior.

name: skillOverrides
description: Hide or collapse a skill without editing its SKILL.md. Claude Code applies the value under each skill's name to the skill list Claude sees and to your / autocomplete.
syntax: skillOverrides: <object mapping skill name to one of:>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented skillOverrides behavior.

name: skipAutoPermissionPrompt
description: Skip the one-time notice describing auto mode that Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself, for example through your own settings or the mode selector, rather than when the built-in default starts a session in it. Claude Code shows that notice once and then records that it was shown, so this key only matters where the notice hasn't appeared yet.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented skipAutoPermissionPrompt behavior.

name: skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt
description: Skip the confirmation dialog Claude Code shows before a session enters bypassPermissions mode, whether from --dangerously-skip-permissions or from defaultMode: "bypassPermissions". Claude Code writes true here in your user settings when you accept that dialog once.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt behavior.

name: skipWebFetchPreflight
description: Skip the WebFetch domain safety check, which sends each requested hostname to api.anthropic.com before fetching. Set true in environments that block traffic to Anthropic, such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry deployments with restrictive egress.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented skipWebFetchPreflight behavior.

name: spellcheck
description: Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using a spell checker you install. Claude Code checks only the text in the input box. Check spelling as you type covers installing aspell, hunspell, or ispell and what the checker covers. Requires Claude Code v2.1.235 or later.
syntax: spellcheck: <object with enabled (Boolean), checker ("aspell", "hunspell", "ispell", or "auto"), language (string, passed to the checker as its dictionary name), and color (string, a terminal color name, #rrggbb, rgb(r,g,b), ansi256(n), or ansi:)>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented spellcheck behavior.

conditions: Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using a spell checker you install. Claude Code checks only the text in the input box. Check spelling as you type covers installing aspell, hunspell, or ispell and what the checker covers. Requires Claude Code v2.1.235 or later.

name: spinnerTipsEnabled
description: While Claude works, the spinner line rotates through short tips about Claude Code features, such as "Use Plan Mode to prepare for a complex request before making changes. Press Shift+Tab twice to enable." Set this key to false to hide them. Appears in /config as Show tips.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented spinnerTipsEnabled behavior.

name: spinnerTipsOverride
description: Add your own tips to the spinner tips that Claude Code shows while Claude works, or replace the built-in tips with yours. Claude Code puts your tips in the same rotation as the built-in ones: it picks the tip that has gone unshown the longest, skips tips still in their cooldown, and breaks ties by priority.
syntax: spinnerTipsOverride: <object with tips, tipsFile, label, and excludeDefault fields, each optional>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented spinnerTipsOverride behavior.

name: spinnerVerbs
description: While a turn is in progress, the spinner shows a rotating verb such as "Accomplishing", "Architecting", or "Baking". Use this key to add your own verbs to that rotation or replace the built-in list with yours.
syntax: spinnerVerbs: <object with a verbs array of strings and mode, one of:>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented spinnerVerbs behavior.

name: sshConfigs
description: Add SSH connections to the Desktop environment dropdown. Administrators use it to distribute shared connections to a team. Connections you define in managed settings show as managed, so users can select them but can't edit or delete them in the app.
syntax: sshConfigs: <array of objects, each with required id, name, and sshHost and optional sshPort and sshIdentityFile>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sshConfigs behavior.

name: sshHostAllowlist
description: Limit the hosts a Desktop SSH session can connect to. Only the Desktop app reads this key; the CLI doesn't. Patterns are case-insensitive: * matches any host, *.example.com matches example.com and every subdomain, and anything else is an exact match against the hostname after ~/.ssh/config resolution. An empty array turns SSH sessions off.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented sshHostAllowlist behavior.

name: statusLine
description: Run your own command to render a status line below the prompt with context such as the model, cost, or git branch. Optional fields adjust spacing, add periodic re-runs, and hide the built-in vim mode indicator when your script renders vim.mode itself.
syntax: statusLine: <object with type set to "command" and a command string, plus optional padding as a number of characters, refreshInterval as a number of seconds, minimum 1, and hideVimModeIndicator as a Boolean>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented statusLine behavior.

name: strictKnownMarketplaces
description: Restrict which plugin marketplace sources people in your organization can add and install plugins from. Claude Code enforces the allowlist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, before any network or filesystem operation, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins once its source no longer matches. Blocked users see an error naming the managed policy.
syntax: strictKnownMarketplaces: <array of marketplace source objects; see Allowed source types>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented strictKnownMarketplaces behavior.

name: strictPluginOnlyCustomization
description: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can come only from plugins or managed settings. Combine it with strictKnownMarketplaces to control the full customization supply chain: the marketplace allowlist controls which plugins users can install.
syntax: strictPluginOnlyCustomization: <true to lock all four kinds of customization, or an array naming the kinds to lock, from "skills", "agents", "hooks", and "mcp">
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented strictPluginOnlyCustomization behavior.

name: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.agents
description: Lock the agents surface. Claude Code stops loading agents from ~/.claude/agents/ and .claude/agents/, and keeps loading plugin agents, built-in agents, and agents in the managed policy directory.
syntax: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.agents: <the string "agents" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented strictPluginOnlyCustomization.agents behavior.

name: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.hooks
description: Lock the hooks surface. Claude Code stops running hooks from user, project, and local settings.json, and keeps running plugin hooks and hooks in managed settings.
syntax: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.hooks: <the string "hooks" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented strictPluginOnlyCustomization.hooks behavior.

name: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.mcp
description: Lock the mcp surface. Claude Code stops loading MCP servers from ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json, and keeps loading plugin MCP servers and managed-mcp.json servers.
syntax: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.mcp: <the string "mcp" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented strictPluginOnlyCustomization.mcp behavior.

name: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.skills
description: Lock the skills surface. Claude Code stops loading skills from ~/.claude/skills/ and .claude/skills/, custom commands from ~/.claude/commands/ and .claude/commands/, skills under --add-dir directories, and skills synced from your claude.ai account, and keeps loading plugin skills, bundled skills, and skills in the managed policy directory.
syntax: strictPluginOnlyCustomization.skills: <the string "skills" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented strictPluginOnlyCustomization.skills behavior.

name: subagentPromptCacheTtl
description: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the requests Claude Code makes outside the main conversation. This key applies to subagents, workflows, and Claude Code's own background and helper requests, such as compaction and session titles. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented subagentPromptCacheTtl behavior.

conditions: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the requests Claude Code makes outside the main conversation. This key applies to subagents, workflows, and Claude Code's own background and helper requests, such as compaction and session titles. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

name: subagentStatusLine
description: When Claude runs subagents, Claude Code lists them in a task display below the prompt, one row per subagent showing name · description · token count. This key lets you run your own command to rewrite those rows, for example to show each subagent's context usage as a percentage. On each refresh, Claude Code sends the visible rows as one JSON object on stdin, with a tasks array carrying each subagent's id, name, status, model, tokenCount, and more, and replaces the row for each id you write back as a {"id", "content"} line. Rows you don't write back keep the default rendering.
syntax: subagentStatusLine: <object with type set to "command" and a command string>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented subagentStatusLine behavior.

name: switchModelsOnFlag
description: Choose what happens when a safety classifier flags a request: switch to the fallback model and continue, or pause so you can choose between switching and editing the prompt.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented switchModelsOnFlag behavior.

name: syncClaudeAiSkills
description: Turn off the download of the skills you enable on claude.ai. Claude Code downloads them into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ when you run it in non-interactive mode with the -p flag and CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS set. Set false to stop that download and hide the skills it already synced. Claude Code honors only false: true is the same as unset and doesn't turn syncing on.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented syncClaudeAiSkills behavior.

name: syntaxHighlightingDisabled
description: Claude Code colors code by language in the diffs, code blocks, and file previews it shows in the terminal, with its built-in highlighter; no plugin or language server is involved. Set this key to true to show them as plain text instead, for example if the colors clash with your terminal theme or slow a screen reader.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented syntaxHighlightingDisabled behavior.

name: teammateDefaultModel
description: Removed in v2.1.234, together with its /config row Default teammate model. Setting it has no effect on current versions.
syntax: teammateDefaultModel: <string, a model alias or full model ID, or null>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented teammateDefaultModel behavior.

name: teammateMode
description: Choose where Claude Code shows agent team teammates: inside your main terminal pane, or in split panes when your terminal supports them. See Choose a display mode.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented teammateMode behavior.

name: terminalProgressBarEnabled
description: Some terminals can show a progress indicator on the tab or in the taskbar for the program running in them. While Claude is working, Claude Code reports an in-progress state to the terminal and clears it when the turn ends, so you can see from another tab or window whether Claude is still busy. It does so only in terminals that support the indicator: ConEmu, Ghostty 1.2.0 or later, and iTerm2 3.6.6 or later. Set this key to false to stop reporting it. Appears in /config as Terminal progress bar.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented terminalProgressBarEnabled behavior.

name: terminalTitleFromRename
description: Claude Code sets your terminal tab's title. By default it uses a title it generates from the conversation, and once you give the session a name with /rename or --name, the tab shows that name instead. Set this key to false to keep the generated title on the tab even after you name the session. The name itself still applies, so /resume and the session picker find it.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented terminalTitleFromRename behavior.

name: theme
description: Pick the color theme for the interface. Appears in /config as Theme.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented theme behavior.

name: tui
description: Choose the terminal UI renderer. Use "fullscreen" for the flicker-free alt-screen renderer with virtualized scrollback, or "default" for the classic main-screen renderer. Running /tui fullscreen or /tui default writes this key for you.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented tui behavior.

name: ultracode
description: Start sessions with ultracode on. With it on, Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task instead of waiting for you to ask. Claude plans workflows only when dynamic workflows are enabled for you and your model supports xhigh effort. Either way, ultracode: true runs the session at xhigh effort. Claude Code reads this key but never writes it: /effort ultracode turns ultracode on for the current session only.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented ultracode behavior.

name: useAutoModeDuringPlan
description: Choose whether Claude Code uses the auto mode classifier to review shell commands in plan mode. With the default true, the classifier reviews each command during planning when auto mode is available and you see no prompt. Set false to get a permission prompt for every command outside the built-in read-only set. Appears in /config as Use auto mode during plan.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented useAutoModeDuringPlan behavior.

name: verbose
description: By default, the transcript collapses each tool call to a short summary, such as the command Claude ran and a line count of its output, and you press Ctrl+O to switch the whole transcript to the expanded view when you want the details. Set this key to true to show every tool call's full input and output inline as it happens, which is useful when you're debugging a hook, an MCP server, or a long shell command. Appears in /config as Verbose output.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented verbose behavior.

name: viewMode
description: Set the transcript view Claude Code starts in: "default", "verbose", or "focus". When set, it overrides both the sticky /focus selection and the verbose setting.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented viewMode behavior.

name: vimInsertModeRemaps
description: Map two-key INSERT-mode sequences to Escape in vim editor mode. Each key is exactly two printable characters typed in sequence, and "" is the only supported target; Claude Code ignores other entries. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later.
syntax: vimInsertModeRemaps: <object mapping a two-character sequence to "">
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented vimInsertModeRemaps behavior.

conditions: Map two-key INSERT-mode sequences to Escape in vim editor mode. Each key is exactly two printable characters typed in sequence, and "" is the only supported target; Claude Code ignores other entries. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later.

name: voice
description: Turn on voice dictation and choose how the dictation key behaves. Claude Code writes this object for you when you run /voice.
syntax: voice: <object with enabled as a Boolean, autoSubmit as a Boolean that applies in hold mode only, and mode, one of:>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented voice behavior.

name: voiceEnabled
description: Deprecated since v2.1.92, when the voice object replaced it. Claude Code still reads it so older settings files keep working, but new configurations should set voice.enabled.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented voiceEnabled behavior.
when_not_to_use: Avoid this deprecated setting in new configuration; use the documented replacement when available.

name: wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled
description: Accelerate mouse-wheel scroll speed during fast scrolls in fullscreen rendering. Set it to false for a constant scroll rate per wheel notch. Requires Claude Code v2.1.174 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled behavior.

conditions: Accelerate mouse-wheel scroll speed during fast scrolls in fullscreen rendering. Set it to false for a constant scroll rate per wheel notch. Requires Claude Code v2.1.174 or later.

name: workflowKeywordTriggerEnabled
description: Choose whether typing the keyword ultracode in a prompt triggers a dynamic workflow. Set it to false to type the word without triggering one. Requires Claude Code v2.1.157 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented workflowKeywordTriggerEnabled behavior.

conditions: Choose whether typing the keyword ultracode in a prompt triggers a dynamic workflow. Set it to false to type the word without triggering one. Requires Claude Code v2.1.157 or later.

name: workflowSizeGuideline
description: Set the agent count Claude aims for in the dynamic workflows it writes. Claude Code sends the value to Claude as advice, not an enforced cap: "small" asks for fewer than 5 agents, "medium" fewer than 15, and "large" fewer than 50. Choose "small" when you want to bound what a workflow spends. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented workflowSizeGuideline behavior.

conditions: Set the agent count Claude aims for in the dynamic workflows it writes. Claude Code sends the value to Claude as advice, not an enforced cap: "small" asks for fewer than 5 agents, "medium" fewer than 15, and "large" fewer than 50. Choose "small" when you want to bound what a workflow spends. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

name: worktree
description: Configure how Claude Code creates and manages git worktrees for --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, and isolated subagents and background sessions.
syntax: worktree: <object with baseRef, symlinkDirectories, sparsePaths, and bgIsolation>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented worktree behavior.

name: worktree.baseRef
description: Choose which ref new worktrees branch from. "fresh" branches from origin/ for a clean tree matching the remote; "head" branches from your current local HEAD, so unpushed commits and feature-branch state are present in the worktree.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented worktree.baseRef behavior.

name: worktree.bgIsolation
description: Choose how background sessions isolate their file edits. With "worktree", Claude Code blocks Edit and Write in the main checkout until the session calls EnterWorktree; with "none", background jobs edit the working copy directly. Set "none" for a repository where git worktrees are impractical.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented worktree.bgIsolation behavior.

name: worktree.sparsePaths
description: Check out only the listed directories in each worktree through git sparse-checkout. Claude Code writes only those directories plus root-level files to disk, which is faster in large monorepos; see Check out only the directories you need.
syntax: worktree.sparsePaths: <array of strings, directory paths relative to the repository root>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented worktree.sparsePaths behavior.

name: worktree.symlinkDirectories
description: Symlink directories from the main repository into each worktree so you don't duplicate large directories on disk.
syntax: worktree.symlinkDirectories: <array of strings, directory paths relative to the repository root>
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented worktree.symlinkDirectories behavior.

name: wslInheritsWindowsSettings
description: Have Claude Code on WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain, with HKLM and the Windows managed settings file taking priority over /etc/claude-code and HKCU below it. While the chain is on, Claude Code reads /etc/claude-code only when no managed settings file or drop-in under C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\ delivers a policy key. Set it to extend the policy you already deploy on Windows to WSL sessions on the same machine, so they follow the same rules as host sessions. Claude Code honors it only when set in the HKLM registry key or in a managed settings file or drop-in under C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\, both of which require Windows admin to write.
when_to_use: Set this option when you need the documented wslInheritsWindowsSettings behavior.
