conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN
role: Claude Code Resume Interrupted Turn configuration
description: Set to 1 to automatically resume if the previous session ended mid-turn. Used in SDK mode so the model continues without requiring the SDK to re-send the prompt. To turn this off, unset the variable or set it to 0. Before v2.1.221, Claude Code ignored 0 and other falsy values, so setting 0 still triggered the resume in non-interactive mode and unsetting the variable was the only way to turn it off

conditions: if the previous session ended mid-turn.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS
display_name: Claude Code Resume Interrupted Turn Max Age Ms
role: Claude Code Resume Interrupted Turn Max Age Ms configuration
description: Maximum age in milliseconds of the last transcript message for a session that ended mid-turn to continue automatically on resume. When the last message is older than this bound, Claude Code skips both the CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN automatic resume and the injected CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT continuation message, and the session starts idle so you continue explicitly. Unset or 0 means no bound; a negative or non-numeric value applies a one-hour bound. Spawn scripts for long-running agents can set this so a restart against an old transcript doesn't re-run a stale prompt. Claude Code sets a one-hour bound itself when it restarts a crashed agent view session that inherited its conversation from an interactive session. Requires Claude Code v2.1.211 or later

conditions: When the last message is older than this bound, Claude Code skips both the CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN automatic resume and the injected CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT continuation message, and the session starts idle so you continue explicitly.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT
description: Override the continuation message injected when resuming a session that ended mid-turn. Defaults to Continue from where you left off.. Spawn scripts for long-running agents can set this to a more directive boot message. An empty string uses the default

conditions: when resuming a session that ended mid-turn.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG
description: Set to 1 for unattended sessions such as eval harnesses, CI jobs, or remote workers. Retries 429 and 529 capacity errors indefinitely instead of failing after CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES attempts. Claude Code fails at once on a 429 that reports a spend limit or exhausted usage credits, even one from a gateway spend cap that resets on a schedule. Before v2.1.239, the watchdog retried these indefinitely. The watchdog backs off up to 5 minutes between attempts, or until the limit resets when the response carries a rate-limit reset time, so a session that hits a usage limit waits out the remaining window. On v2.1.199 or later it also raises the default retry count for other transient errors, such as server errors, timeouts, and dropped connections, to 300, roughly three hours of backoff, and removes the cap of 15 on CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES if you set that variable explicitly. Requires Claude Code v2.1.186 or later

conditions: when the response carries a rate-limit reset time, so a session that hits a usage limit waits out the remaining window.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE
description: Set to 1 to start in safe mode: CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands and agents, output styles, workflows, custom themes, custom keybindings, status line and file-suggestion commands, LSP servers, and auto memory do not load, for troubleshooting a broken configuration. Managed settings policy still applies, including policy-configured hooks, status line, and file-suggestion commands; managed plugins, managed skills, managed CLAUDE.md, and policy-configured MCP servers do not. Equivalent to passing --safe-mode. Directly spawned child processes inherit the variable

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SCRIPT_CAPS
description: JSON object limiting how many times specific scripts may be invoked per session when CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set. Keys are substrings matched against the command text; values are integer call limits. For example, {"deploy.sh": 2} allows deploy.sh to be called at most twice. Matching is substring-based so shell-expansion tricks like ./scripts/deploy.sh $(evil) still count against the cap. Runtime fan-out via xargs or find -exec is not detected; this is a defense-in-depth control

conditions: when CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SCROLL_SPEED
description: Set the mouse wheel scroll multiplier in fullscreen rendering. Accepts any positive value up to 20, including fractional values below 1 such as 0.5 to slow accelerated trackpad and wheel scrolling in terminals that already amplify wheel events. Set to 3 to match vim if your terminal sends one wheel event per notch without amplification. Ignored in the JetBrains IDE terminal, where Claude Code uses its own scroll handling

conditions: if your terminal sends one wheel event per notch without amplification.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK
description: Set to 0 to turn off Claude-drafted feedback for a session. Set to 1 to turn it on where your account already has access; the variable can't grant access itself, and the other switches that turn feedback off, such as DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND and the feedbackDrafts setting's off value, still apply

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Code Sessionend Hooks Timeout Ms
role: Claude Code Sessionend Hooks Timeout Ms configuration
description: Override the time budget in milliseconds for SessionEnd hooks. Applies to session exit, /clear, and switching sessions via interactive /resume. By default the budget is 1.5 seconds, automatically raised to the highest per-hook timeout configured in settings files, up to 60 seconds. Timeouts on plugin-provided hooks do not raise the budget

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
description: Set automatically to the current session ID in Bash and PowerShell tool subprocesses, hook command subprocesses, and stdio MCP server subprocesses. For Bash, PowerShell, and hooks this matches the session_id field in the hook JSON input and is updated on /clear. An MCP server subprocess retains the ID it was spawned with. On --resume it receives the resumed ID, matching hooks and Bash. On --continue or --resume without an explicit ID it may receive the initial startup ID instead. Use to correlate scripts and external tools with the Claude Code session that launched them

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL
description: Set the shell Claude Code uses to run Bash tool commands. Accepts a path to a bash or zsh binary, for example /opt/homebrew/bin/bash. Other shells such as fish are not supported. If the value is not a working bash or zsh path, Claude Code ignores it and falls back to auto-detection. Auto-detection uses your $SHELL when it points to bash or zsh, otherwise it picks the first working zsh then bash found on your PATH and standard install locations

conditions: If the value is not a working bash or zsh path, Claude Code ignores it and falls back to auto-detection.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX
description: Command prefix that wraps shell commands Claude Code spawns: Bash tool calls, hook commands, status line commands, and stdio MCP server startup commands. PowerShell hooks and exec-form hooks run without the prefix. Useful for logging or auditing. Setting a bare executable path such as /path/to/logger.sh runs each command as /path/to/logger.sh ''. The wrapper receives the command line as a single shell-quoted argument in $1, so the wrapper must re-evaluate $1 with a shell, for example exec bash -c "$1". Treating $1 as a bare executable path breaks stdio MCP servers that pass arguments such as npx -y . For Bash tool calls, $1 contains the full shell invocation Claude Code assembles, including environment setup, not only the command Claude ran

conditions: Availability depends on the documented provider, platform, version, or execution mode.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE
description: Set to 1 to run with a minimal system prompt and only the Bash, file read, and file edit tools. MCP tools from --mcp-config are still available. Disables auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md. Skills in a directory you pass with --add-dir still load. OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read, so Anthropic authentication must come from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper in --settings. Equivalent to passing --bare

conditions: available.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT
role: Claude Code Simple System Prompt configuration
description: Set to 1 to use a shorter system prompt and abbreviated tool descriptions on any model. Set to 0, false, no, or off to opt out even on models where the experiment or server configuration would otherwise enable it. The full tool set, hooks, MCP servers, and CLAUDE.md discovery remain enabled

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_ANTHROPIC_AWS_AUTH
display_name: Claude Code Skip Anthropic Aws Auth
role: Claude Code Skip Anthropic Aws Auth configuration
description: Skip client-side authentication for Claude Platform on AWS, for gateways that sign requests themselves

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_AWS_CRED_CACHE
display_name: Claude Code Skip Aws Cred Cache
role: Claude Code Skip Aws Cred Cache configuration
description: Set to 1 to turn off the in-process cache of credentials resolved from the AWS default credential provider chain, so Claude Code resolves the chain on every API request. With the cache off, an SSO-backed profile requests credentials from IAM Identity Center on every request. See credential caching and resolution timeout. Requires Claude Code v2.1.207 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH
role: Claude Code Skip Bedrock Auth configuration
description: Skip AWS authentication for Amazon Bedrock (for example, when using an LLM gateway)

conditions: when using an LLM gateway)

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FAST_MODE_NETWORK_ERRORS
display_name: Claude Code Skip Fast Mode Network Errors
role: Claude Code Skip Fast Mode Network Errors configuration
description: Set to 1 to treat a failed fast mode availability check as available, for networks that block the check's direct request to api.anthropic.com. Claude Code still honors a "disabled by your organization" response

conditions: available, for networks that block the check's direct request to api.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FAST_MODE_ORG_CHECK
display_name: Claude Code Skip Fast Mode Org Check
role: Claude Code Skip Fast Mode Org Check configuration
description: Set to 1 to skip the client-side fast mode availability check, for proxies that intercept the check's request rather than refuse it. The API still rejects fast mode requests when your organization has fast mode disabled

conditions: when your organization has fast mode disabled

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FOUNDRY_AUTH
role: Claude Code Skip Foundry Auth configuration
description: Skip Azure authentication for Microsoft Foundry, for a proxy or gateway that injects its own Authorization header. Claude Code sends requests without an Azure credential and preserves the Authorization header you supply, for example through ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS. Ignored when ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_AUTH_TOKEN is set. Before v2.1.203, this variable left the Microsoft Foundry client unable to send requests unless an API key was also set

conditions: when ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_AUTH_TOKEN is set.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH
role: Claude Code Skip Mantle Auth configuration
description: Skip AWS authentication for Amazon Bedrock Mantle (for example, when using an LLM gateway)

conditions: when using an LLM gateway)

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY
role: Claude Code Skip Prompt History configuration
description: Set to 1 to skip writing prompt history and session transcripts to disk. Sessions started with this variable set do not appear in --resume, --continue, or up-arrow history. Useful for ephemeral scripted sessions

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_VERTEX_AUTH
role: Claude Code Skip Vertex Auth configuration
description: Skip Google authentication for Google Cloud's Agent Platform (for example, when using an LLM gateway)

conditions: when using an LLM gateway)

name: CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP
display_name: Claude Code Stop Hook Block Cap
role: Claude Code Stop Hook Block Cap configuration
description: Maximum number of consecutive times a Stop or SubagentStop hook may block the turn from ending before Claude Code overrides it and ends the turn anyway (default: 8). Set to 0 to disable the cap. Raise this if your hook legitimately needs more iterations to resolve

conditions: if your hook legitimately needs more iterations to resolve

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL
description: The model Claude Code uses for all subagents, agent teams, and agents in a workflow. Accepts an alias such as haiku or a full model name, and takes precedence over the per-invocation model parameter and the subagent definition's model frontmatter. See Model configuration. Setting it to inherit is the same as leaving it unset; before v2.1.196, inherit was an override that forced every subagent onto the main conversation's model

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL
display_name: Claude Code Subagent Prompt Cache Ttl
role: Claude Code Subagent Prompt Cache Ttl configuration
description: Set 5m or 1h, the only values Claude Code accepts, to choose the prompt cache TTL for requests outside the main conversation, such as subagents, workflows, and background work. Takes precedence over the subagentPromptCacheTtl setting and over ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M overrides it. The API bills 1-hour cache writes at a higher rate. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB
role: Claude Code Subprocess Env Scrub configuration
description: Set to 1 to strip Anthropic and cloud provider credentials from subprocess environments (Bash tool, hooks, MCP stdio servers). The parent Claude process keeps these credentials for API calls, but child processes cannot read them, reducing exposure to prompt injection attacks that attempt to exfiltrate secrets via shell expansion. On Linux, this also runs Bash subprocesses in an isolated PID namespace so they cannot read host process environments via /proc; as a side effect, ps, pgrep, and kill cannot see or signal host processes. claude-code-action sets this automatically when allowed_non_write_users is configured

conditions: when allowed_non_write_users is configured

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL
role: Claude Code Sync Plugin Install configuration
description: Set to 1 in non-interactive mode (the -p flag) to wait for plugin installation to complete before the first query. Without this, plugins install in the background and may not be available on the first turn. Combine with CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS to bound the wait

conditions: available on the first turn.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Code Sync Plugin Install Timeout Ms
role: Claude Code Sync Plugin Install Timeout Ms configuration
description: Timeout in milliseconds for synchronous plugin installation. When exceeded, Claude Code proceeds without plugins and logs an error. No default: without this variable, synchronous installation waits until complete

conditions: When exceeded, Claude Code proceeds without plugins and logs an error.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS
description: Set to 1 to download your enabled claude.ai skills into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ and resync every 10 minutes. Before it runs the first query, Claude Code waits up to CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS for the list of your skills. The downloads themselves finish in the background, and Claude waits for a skill's download when it invokes that skill. The synced folder name is reserved for this download. Before v2.1.227, the skills downloaded into ~/.claude/skills/ directly. Applies only in non-interactive mode with the -p flag. Requires claude.ai authentication. Claude Code on the web sessions receive your enabled claude.ai skills automatically; you don't need to set this there. Claude Code applies extra rules to the downloaded skills, such as not running their ! commands on your machine

conditions: when it invokes that skill.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Code Sync Skills Install Timeout Ms
role: Claude Code Sync Skills Install Timeout Ms configuration
description: Timeout in milliseconds for a mid-session skills resync when CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS is set (default: 30000). Bounds the download triggered when the host requests a skill reload during the session. When exceeded, the resync stops and remaining downloads continue in the background

conditions: when CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS is set (default: 30000).

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Code Sync Skills Wait Timeout Ms
role: Claude Code Sync Skills Wait Timeout Ms configuration
description: Timeout in milliseconds for the first query to wait for the initial skill list when CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS is set (default: 5000). When exceeded, the first query runs with whichever skills have arrived. The downloads finish in the background either way, and Claude waits for a skill's download when it invokes that skill

conditions: when CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS is set (default: 5000).

name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNTAX_HIGHLIGHT
description: Set to false to disable syntax highlighting in diff output. Useful when colors interfere with your terminal setup. To also disable highlighting in code blocks and file previews, use the syntaxHighlightingDisabled setting

conditions: when colors interfere with your terminal setup.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID
role: Claude Code Task List Id configuration
description: Share a task list across sessions. Set the same ID in multiple Claude Code instances to coordinate on a shared task list, in sessions that have the Task tools. See Task list

name: CLAUDE_CODE_TEAM_TEARDOWN_PARK_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Code Team Teardown Park Timeout Ms
role: Claude Code Team Teardown Park Timeout Ms configuration
description: Override, in milliseconds, how long a non-interactive session waits at exit for its agent team to finish tearing down. Accepts 1000 to 60000; an out-of-range value is ignored and the default of 10000 applies. Requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR
description: Override the temp directory used for internal temp files. Claude Code appends /claude-{uid}/ on Unix or /claude/ on Windows to this path. Default: /tmp on macOS, os.tmpdir() on Linux and Windows. As of v2.1.161, on macOS and Linux, sandboxed Bash subprocesses receive a short fallback $TMPDIR under the system default when your override is a long path, since some tools fail when temp paths get too long. Unsandboxed Bash commands inherit your shell's $TMPDIR unchanged. Claude Code's own temp files always use your override

conditions: when your override is a long path, since some tools fail when temp paths get too long.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_TMUX_TRUECOLOR
description: Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to allow 24-bit truecolor output inside tmux. Setting it to 0 or false still allows truecolor, unlike most on/off variables; unset the variable to restore the 256-color clamp. By default, Claude Code clamps to 256 colors when $TMUX is set because tmux does not pass through truecolor escape sequences unless configured to. Set this after adding set -ga terminal-overrides ',*:Tc' to your ~/.tmux.conf. See Terminal configuration for other tmux settings

conditions: when $TMUX is set because tmux does not pass through truecolor escape sequences unless configured to.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_CGROUP_EXCLUDE
display_name: Claude Code Tool Memory Cgroup Exclude
role: Claude Code Tool Memory Cgroup Exclude configuration
description: On Linux and WSL, set to a comma-separated list of the kinds of processes Claude Code excludes from the tool memory cap, such as mcp or lsp. Set none to cap every kind, or all-new to cap only Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor tool commands. Claude Code keeps Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor tool commands under the cap whatever you list. Requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT
role: Claude Code Tool Memory Limit configuration
description: On Linux and WSL, set to a size such as 4G to cap the memory that Bash and PowerShell tool commands can use, and Monitor tool commands on v2.1.246 or later. Write the size in plain digits, alone for a number of bytes or with a K, M, G, or T suffix. Set 0 or off to turn the cap off. Once the first process Claude Code starts has turned the cap on or off, a changed value takes effect the next time you launch claude. Requires Claude Code v2.1.233 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USER_DIALOG_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Code User Dialog Timeout Ms
role: Claude Code User Dialog Timeout Ms configuration
description: Deadline in milliseconds for dialogs Claude Code forwards to a remote client, such as a Remote Control or SDK host, and for the approval dialog for a held cross-session message, before Claude Code cancels them; permission prompts and AskUserQuestion questions use their own flows and aren't governed by it. Also bounds the mid-session Fable 5 usage-credits consent prompt in a session that may be running unattended. Control inbound messages and non-interactive sessions cover the full held-message expiry rules, including the cases where the deadline doesn't apply. Overrides the dialogExpiry setting; 0 or a negative value disables the deadline

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS
role: Claude Code Use Anthropic Aws configuration
description: Use Claude Platform on AWS

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK
description: Use Amazon Bedrock

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY
description: Use Microsoft Foundry

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE
description: Use the Amazon Bedrock Mantle endpoint

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_NATIVE_FILE_SEARCH
display_name: Claude Code Use Native File Search
role: Claude Code Use Native File Search configuration
description: Set to 1 to discover custom commands, subagents, and output styles using Node.js file APIs instead of ripgrep. Set this if the bundled ripgrep binary is unavailable or blocked in your environment. Does not affect the Grep or file search tools

conditions: if the bundled ripgrep binary is unavailable or blocked in your environment.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL
role: Claude Code Use Powershell Tool configuration
description: Controls the PowerShell tool. On Windows without Git Bash, the tool is enabled automatically; set to 0 to disable it. On Windows with Git Bash installed, the tool is on by default for claude.ai and Console accounts; set to 1 to enable it in Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry sessions, or 0 to turn it off. On Linux, macOS, and WSL, set to 1 to enable it, which requires pwsh on your PATH. When enabled on Windows, Claude can run PowerShell commands natively instead of routing through Git Bash. See PowerShell tool

conditions: requires pwsh on your PATH.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX
description: Use Google Cloud's Agent Platform

name: CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS
display_name: Claude Code Webfetch Cache Ttl Ms
role: Claude Code Webfetch Cache Ttl Ms configuration
description: Set to the number of milliseconds WebFetch keeps each fetched URL's response cached. The default is 900000, which is 15 minutes. Takes plain digits only; 0, a decimal, or any other spelling keeps the default. Claude Code reads the value once per launch, so a change in a settings env block applies when you next launch claude. Requires Claude Code v2.1.233 or later

conditions: when you next launch claude.

name: CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS
display_name: Claude Code Workflow Prefix Stagger Ms
role: Claude Code Workflow Prefix Stagger Ms configuration
description: Upper bound in milliseconds on how long a workflow agent waits for a same-prefix sibling's first response to begin before sending its own first request. When a fan-out starts several agents that share a prompt-cache prefix, Claude Code holds all but the first agent for up to this long so the rest read the cached prefix instead of each processing it uncached. Default 5000. Set to 0 to disable the wait. When DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING is set, agents never wait. Requires Claude Code v2.1.229 or later

conditions: When a fan-out starts several agents that share a prompt-cache prefix, Claude Code holds all but the first agent for up to this long so the rest read the cached prefix instead of each processing it uncached.

name: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
description: Override the configuration directory (default: ~/.claude). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path, as are credentials on Linux and Windows; on macOS, credentials are in the system Keychain. Useful for running multiple accounts side by side: for example, alias claude-work='CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work claude'

name: CLAUDE_DISABLE_ADOPT
description: Set to 1 to stop in-flight background work instead of carrying it over when you background a session by pressing ← or with /background. Claude Code asks you to confirm before backgrounding, then stops the tasks that would otherwise carry over. Requires Claude Code v2.1.195 or later

conditions: when you background a session by pressing ← or with /background.

name: CLAUDE_EFFORT
description: Set automatically in Bash tool subprocesses and hook commands to the effort level in effect when the subprocess starts: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max. Ultracode is not a distinct level and reports as xhigh. Matches the effort.level field passed to hooks. Only set when the current model supports the effort parameter

conditions: when the subprocess starts: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max.

name: CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG
description: Set to 1 to force-enable the byte-level streaming idle watchdog, or set to 0 to force-disable it. 0 also turns off the first-byte deadline on the connections where that deadline runs. When unset, the watchdog is enabled by default for direct Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS connections, and for streaming responses on gateway connections reached through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL; before v2.1.222 it didn't run on those gateway connections, so the event-level watchdog could report a stall there even while keep-alive pings were arriving. For timeouts and how the timers interact, see Streaming idle watchdogs

conditions: When unset, the watchdog is enabled by default for direct Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS connections, and for streaming responses on gateway connections reached through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL; before v2.

name: CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG_BEDROCK
role: Claude Enable Byte Watchdog Bedrock configuration
description: Set to 1 to enable the byte-level streaming idle watchdog on Amazon Bedrock vnd.amazon.eventstream responses, which also enables the first-byte deadline on Bedrock streaming requests. Off by default. Configure the timeout with CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS

name: CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG
description: Set to 0 to force-disable the event-level streaming idle watchdog, or set to 1 to force-enable it. When unset, the watchdog is on by default for all providers. Before v2.1.196, the unset default was server-controlled on the direct Anthropic API and off on other providers. Configure the timeout with CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS; for the other stall timers that run alongside this one, see Streaming idle watchdogs

conditions: When unset, the watchdog is on by default for all providers.

name: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
description: Path to a shell script whose contents Claude Code runs before each Bash command in the same shell process, so exports in the file are visible to the command. Use to persist virtualenv or conda activation across commands. Also populated dynamically by SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged, and FileChanged hooks

name: CLAUDE_PID
description: Claude Code sets this to its own process ID in the subprocesses it spawns: Bash and PowerShell tool commands and hook commands. On Linux, the Bash tool's shell integration uses it to refuse a pkill pattern that would match the Claude Code process itself; see the error reference. Read it from your own scripts to identify or signal the parent Claude Code process deliberately. Requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: CLAUDE_REMOTE_CONTROL_SESSION_NAME_PREFIX
display_name: Claude Remote Control Session Name Prefix
role: Claude Remote Control Session Name Prefix configuration
description: Prefix for auto-generated Remote Control session names when no explicit name is provided. Defaults to your machine's hostname, producing names like myhost-graceful-unicorn. The --remote-control-session-name-prefix CLI flag sets the same value for a single invocation

conditions: when no explicit name is provided.

name: CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS
display_name: Claude Stream First Byte Timeout Ms
role: Claude Stream First Byte Timeout Ms configuration
description: Deadline in milliseconds for the first response byte of a streaming request, on the connections where the first-byte deadline runs. For how Claude Code clamps it, the extra time it adds for large request bodies, and how it picks the deadline when you leave this unset, see No response from API. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later

conditions: when you leave this unset, see No response from API.

name: CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS
role: Claude Stream Idle Timeout Ms configuration
description: Timeout in milliseconds before the event- and byte-level streaming idle watchdogs close a stalled connection. When you set this variable explicitly, the minimum is 300000 (5 minutes); lower values are silently clamped to absorb extended thinking pauses and proxy buffering, and the byte-level watchdog caps the value at 30 minutes. CLAUDE_BYTE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS takes precedence over this variable for the byte-level watchdog. For the per-watchdog unset defaults, see Streaming idle watchdogs

conditions: When you set this variable explicitly, the minimum is 300000 (5 minutes); lower values are silently clamped to absorb extended thinking pauses and proxy buffering, and the byte-level watchdog caps the value at 30 minutes.

name: CLAUDE_SUBAGENT_BG_SHELL_MAX_MS
display_name: Claude Subagent Bg Shell Max Ms
role: Claude Subagent Bg Shell Max Ms configuration
description: Maximum lifetime in milliseconds for a background shell command that a subagent started. Default 3600000 (60 minutes). When you set 0, Claude Code applies the default instead of removing the cap. When the subagent runs in the foreground, Claude Code also ends the command when that subagent gives its final response, regardless of this cap. See the background command lifetime rules. Claude Code doesn't cap main-session background commands this way. For the memory-pressure limit that covers them, see How backgrounding works

conditions: When you set 0, Claude Code applies the default instead of removing the cap.

name: DEBUG
description: Set to 1 to enable debug mode, equivalent to launching with --debug. Debug logs are written to ~/.claude/debug/.txt, or to the path set by CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOGS_DIR. Only the truthy values 1, true, yes, and on enable debug mode, so namespace patterns like DEBUG=express:* set for other tools do not trigger it

conditions: Availability depends on the documented provider, platform, version, or execution mode.

name: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER
description: Set to 1 to disable automatic background updates. Manual claude update still works. Use DISABLE_UPDATES to block both

name: DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT
description: Set to 1 to disable automatic compaction when approaching the context limit. The manual /compact command remains available. Use when you want explicit control over when compaction occurs. Overrides the autoCompactEnabled setting

conditions: when approaching the context limit.

name: DISABLE_COMPACT
description: Set to 1 to disable all compaction: both automatic compaction and the manual /compact command

name: DISABLE_COST_WARNINGS
description: Set to 1 to disable cost warning messages

name: DISABLE_DOCTOR_COMMAND
description: Set to 1 to hide the /doctor setup checkup skill and its /checkup alias. Useful for managed deployments where users shouldn't run setup diagnostics from a session. Doesn't affect the claude doctor terminal command. Before v2.1.205, this variable hid the /doctor diagnostics screen command

name: DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING
description: Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to opt out of error reporting. Setting it to 0 or false still opts out, unlike most on/off variables; unset the variable to turn error reporting back on

name: DISABLE_EXTRA_USAGE_COMMAND
description: Set to 1 to hide the /usage-credits command that lets users purchase additional usage beyond rate limits

name: DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND
description: Set to 1 to disable the /feedback command and Claude-drafted feedback. Also disables /bug and /share, which report through the same path; before v2.1.212 they were aliases of /feedback, so the command was disabled under every name. The older name DISABLE_BUG_COMMAND is also accepted

name: DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK
description: Set to 1 or true to disable GrowthBook feature-flag fetching and use code defaults for every flag. This makes Remote Control and the other features that need feature-flag fetching unavailable. Setting it to 0 or false leaves fetching on. Telemetry event logging stays on unless DISABLE_TELEMETRY is also set

conditions: available.

name: DISABLE_INSTALLATION_CHECKS
description: Set to 1 to disable installation warnings. Use only when manually managing the installation location, as this can mask issues with standard installations

conditions: when manually managing the installation location, as this can mask issues with standard installations

name: DISABLE_INSTALL_GITHUB_APP_COMMAND
role: Disable Install Github App Command configuration
description: Set to 1 to hide the /install-github-app command. Already hidden when using third-party providers (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry)

conditions: when using third-party providers (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry)

name: DISABLE_INTERLEAVED_THINKING
description: Set to 1 to prevent sending the interleaved-thinking beta header. Useful when your LLM gateway or provider does not support interleaved thinking

conditions: when your LLM gateway or provider does not support interleaved thinking

name: DISABLE_LOGIN_COMMAND
description: Set to 1 to hide the /login command. Useful when authentication is handled externally via API keys or apiKeyHelper

conditions: when authentication is handled externally via API keys or apiKeyHelper

name: DISABLE_LOGOUT_COMMAND
description: Set to 1 to hide the /logout command

name: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING
description: Set to 1 to disable prompt caching for all models (takes precedence over per-model settings)

name: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_FABLE
description: Set to 1 to disable prompt caching for Fable models

name: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU
description: Set to 1 to disable prompt caching for Haiku models

name: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_OPUS
description: Set to 1 to disable prompt caching for Opus models

name: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_SONNET
description: Set to 1 to disable prompt caching for Sonnet models

name: DISABLE_TELEMETRY
description: Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to opt out of telemetry. Setting it to 0 or false still opts out, unlike most on/off variables; unset the variable to turn telemetry back on. Telemetry events do not include user data like code, file paths, or bash commands. Also disables feature-flag fetching with the same effect as DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK, which makes Remote Control and the other features that need feature-flag fetching unavailable. See Turn telemetry off for your organization

conditions: available.

name: DISABLE_UPDATES
description: Set to 1 to block all updates including manual claude update and claude install. Stricter than DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER. Use when distributing Claude Code through your own channels and users should not self-update

conditions: when distributing Claude Code through your own channels and users should not self-update

name: DISABLE_UPGRADE_COMMAND
description: Set to 1 to hide the /upgrade command

name: DO_NOT_TRACK
description: Set to 1 to opt out of telemetry, with the same effect as DISABLE_TELEMETRY, including making Remote Control and the other features that need feature-flag fetching unavailable. Claude Code reads this variable as a standard boolean, so 0 leaves telemetry on, and honors it as the cross-tool convention recognized by many developer CLIs

conditions: available.

name: ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS
description: Set to false to stop Claude Code from fetching claude.ai MCP servers. Enabled by default for logged-in users. To disable per-project or per-org, set disableClaudeAiConnectors in settings instead

name: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H
description: Set to 1 to request a 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the default 5 minutes. Intended for API key, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Platform on AWS users. Subscription users within included usage receive the 1-hour TTL automatically on the main conversation. Subscription users drawing on usage credits can set it to keep the 1-hour TTL. 1-hour cache writes are billed at a higher rate. To choose the TTL per request bucket instead, use CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, which take precedence over this variable

name: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H_BEDROCK
description: Deprecated. Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H instead
when_not_to_use: Do not use this variable in new configuration; use the replacement documented by the vendor when one is provided.

name: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH
description: Controls MCP tool search. Unset, Claude Code defers all MCP tools by default. It still loads them upfront on Google Cloud's Agent Platform models earlier than the Claude 4.5 generation, on a Microsoft Foundry deployment hosted on Azure, and when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points to a non-first-party host. true always defers and sends the beta header, except on those same Agent Platform models and Microsoft Foundry deployments; requests fail on proxies that don't support tool_reference. auto loads upfront when tool definitions fit within 10% of context. auto:N sets a custom threshold, such as auto:5 for 5%. false loads all tools upfront. A value you set yourself is ignored when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS is set. Before v2.1.221, Claude Code disabled tool search for all models on Google Cloud's Agent Platform unless you set this variable to true

conditions: when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points to a non-first-party host.

name: FALLBACK_FOR_ALL_PRIMARY_MODELS
role: Fallback For All Primary Models configuration
description: Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to make every model stop retrying with a repeated-overload error when no fallback model is configured. Setting it to 0 or false still enables this, unlike most on/off variables; unset the variable to restore the default retry behavior. Without it, models Claude Code recognizes as Opus, Fable 5, or Mythos models stop retrying this way when you authenticate with an API key or a third-party provider rather than a Claude subscription. As of v2.1.160, a configured fallback model chain triggers on repeated overload errors for any primary model, so this variable does not affect switching to a fallback model

conditions: when no fallback model is configured.

name: FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS
description: Set to 1 to force plugin auto-updates even when the main auto-updater is disabled via DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER

conditions: when the main auto-updater is disabled via DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER

name: FORCE_HYPERLINK
description: Set to 1 to enable clickable OSC 8 hyperlinks when your terminal supports them but isn't auto-detected, or 0 to disable them. When unset, Claude Code enables hyperlinks only when it detects terminal support. Claude Code parses this value as a number, not a Boolean, so a value such as false, no, or off enables hyperlinks rather than disabling them. Claude Code renders the footer PR or merge request badge as a hyperlink even when it can't detect terminal support, such as over SSH. Set 0 to render the badge as plain text

conditions: when your terminal supports them but isn't auto-detected, or 0 to disable them.

name: FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M
description: Set to 1 to force the 5-minute prompt cache TTL even when 1-hour TTL would otherwise apply. Overrides CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, and the promptCacheTtl and subagentPromptCacheTtl settings

conditions: when 1-hour TTL would otherwise apply.

description: Specify HTTPS proxy server for network connections

name: HTTP_PROXY
description: Specify HTTP proxy server for network connections

name: IS_DEMO
description: Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to enable demo mode: hides your email and organization name from the header and /status output, and skips onboarding. Setting it to 0 or false still enables demo mode, unlike most on/off variables; unset the variable to turn it off. Useful when streaming or recording a session

conditions: when streaming or recording a session

name: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS
description: Maximum number of tokens allowed in MCP tool responses. Claude Code displays a warning when output exceeds 10,000 tokens. Tools that declare anthropic/maxResultSizeChars use that character limit for text content instead, but image content from those tools is still subject to this variable (default: 25000)

conditions: when output exceeds 10,000 tokens.

name: MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES
description: Number of times Claude Code retries when the model's response fails validation against the --json-schema in non-interactive mode with the -p flag. The same retry count applies when a workflow subagent's structured output fails validation. Defaults to 5

conditions: when the model's response fails validation against the --json-schema in non-interactive mode with the -p flag.

name: MAX_THINKING_TOKENS
description: Fixed token budget for extended thinking. Claude Code caps it at one token below the request's max output tokens and never below 1,024; see CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS for how that limit is set. When unset and thinking is enabled, models with adaptive reasoning choose their own thinking depth, and other models use the cap. Set to 0 to disable thinking on the Anthropic API, except on Fable 5, which cannot have thinking turned off; on third-party providers, 0 omits the thinking parameter instead. With thinking turned off on the Anthropic API, Claude Code sends effort high instead of a higher level to models it knows don't accept that combination, such as Opus 5. Nonzero values are ignored on adaptive reasoning models unless CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING is set

conditions: When unset and thinking is enabled, models with adaptive reasoning choose their own thinking depth, and other models use the cap.

name: MCP_CLIENT_SECRET
description: OAuth client secret for MCP servers that require pre-configured credentials. Avoids the interactive prompt when adding a server with --client-secret

conditions: when adding a server with --client-secret

name: MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING
description: Controls whether startup waits for MCP servers to connect before the first query. MCP startup is non-blocking by default: servers connect in the background and their tools become available as they finish. Set to 0 to make Claude Code wait for servers to connect before the first query. Servers configured with alwaysLoad: true still make startup wait regardless, except when served from the discovery cache, since their tools must be present when the first prompt is built. In non-interactive mode (-p), Claude Code also waits for still-pending servers before the first turn regardless of this variable, with a longer deadline when you pass --mcp-config explicitly; see that flag's entry for the cached-server exception

conditions: available as they finish.

name: MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS
description: How long blocking MCP startup waits, in milliseconds, for the connection batch before snapshotting the tool list (default: 5000). Applies when MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=0 or for servers marked alwaysLoad: true. Servers still pending at the deadline keep connecting in the background. Distinct from MCP_TIMEOUT, which bounds an individual server's connect attempt

conditions: when MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=0 or for servers marked alwaysLoad: true.

name: MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE
description: Turns the MCP discovery cache on or off. With the cache on, a remote HTTP or SSE server you've used before can show the cached status, and Claude Code connects it on its first tool call instead of at startup. The cache is off by default unless a gradual rollout has enabled it for your account. Set to 1 to turn it on, or 0 to keep it off even when the rollout has enabled it. Before v2.1.238, the cache was on by default. The cached status requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

conditions: when the rollout has enabled it.

name: MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_STALE_S
display_name: Mcp Discovery Cache Max Stale S
role: Mcp Discovery Cache Max Stale S configuration
description: Maximum age, in seconds, of a discovery-cache entry (default: 14400, or 4 hours). At a start where the entry is older than that, Claude Code discards it and connects the server at startup, as it does with the cache off. Claude Code caps the value at 7 days. Before v2.1.238, the default was 86400, or 24 hours, and Claude Code didn't cap the value

name: MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_STRIKES
description: At a start where a discovery-cache entry is older than MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_S, Claude Code refreshes it in the background. This variable sets how many refreshes in a row can fail before Claude Code discards the entry and connects the server at the next start instead (default: 1). Raise it if your network connection drops occasionally, so that one failed refresh doesn't discard the entry. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later

conditions: if your network connection drops occasionally, so that one failed refresh doesn't discard the entry.

name: MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_S
role: Mcp Discovery Cache Ttl S configuration
description: Seconds for which Claude Code uses a discovery-cache entry without refreshing it (default: 900). At a start where the entry is older than that, Claude Code still uses it but refreshes it in the background. Once the entry is older than MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_STALE_S, Claude Code discards it instead. Claude Code caps the value at MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_STALE_S, which is 4 hours by default. Before v2.1.238, Claude Code didn't cap the value

name: MCP_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT
description: Fixed port for the OAuth redirect callback, as an alternative to --callback-port when adding an MCP server with pre-configured credentials

conditions: when adding an MCP server with pre-configured credentials

name: MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION
description: On the v2 MCP client runtime only, whether Claude Code probes servers for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28. Set auto to probe HTTP, claude.ai connector, and stdio servers; a server that doesn't answer the probe connects on the earlier protocol instead, as SSE and WebSocket servers always do. Set legacy to skip the probe for every server. Without the variable, Claude Code probes HTTP and claude.ai connector servers on Claude Code v2.1.232 or later, with the exceptions the MCP client runtimes section lists. Any other value is ignored with a warning in the debug log. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

conditions: Requires Claude Code v2.

name: MCP_REMOTE_SERVER_CONNECTION_BATCH_SIZE
display_name: Mcp Remote Server Connection Batch Size
role: Mcp Remote Server Connection Batch Size configuration
description: Maximum number of remote MCP servers (HTTP/SSE) to connect in parallel during startup (default: 20)

name: MCP_SDK_GENERATION
description: Pin which MCP client runtime this process connects to MCP servers with: v1, built on MCP TypeScript SDK 1.x, or v2, built on MCP TypeScript SDK 2.0. Without the variable, Claude Code uses v2 on Claude Code v2.1.232 or later, except where that section says it uses v1. On Claude Code v2.1.221 or later, the v2 runtime checks the issuer an MCP OAuth server returns in its authorization response and fails the sign-in with an error that begins Issuer mismatch in authorization response when it doesn't match. The v1 runtime doesn't run this check. If you set an unrecognized value, Claude Code ignores it and writes a warning to the debug log. Claude Code reads the value once per process. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later

conditions: when it doesn't match.

name: MCP_SERVER_CONNECTION_BATCH_SIZE
role: Mcp Server Connection Batch Size configuration
description: Maximum number of local MCP servers (stdio) to connect in parallel during startup (default: 3)

name: MCP_TIMEOUT
description: Timeout in milliseconds for MCP server startup (default: 30000, or 30 seconds)

name: MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT
description: Timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool execution (default: 100000000, about 28 hours). For an HTTP, SSE, or claude.ai connector server, each request also times out after 60 seconds by default; set this variable, or the per-server timeout, above 60000 to raise that per-request limit. A lower value still shortens the overall tool-execution timeout but leaves the per-request limit at 60 seconds. Stdio and WebSocket servers have no per-request timer. A per-server timeout field in .mcp.json overrides this for that server. A per-server timeout of at least 1000 also sets the minimum idle window for that server's tool calls, so CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT never aborts them sooner; this floor requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. For the env variable, values below 1000 are floored to one second; for the per-server field, values below 1000 are ignored

conditions: requires Claude Code v2.

name: OTEL_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT

name: CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT
description: Specifies the endpoint for the code assist server. This is useful for development and testing. ### Environment variable redaction To prevent accidental leakage of sensitive information, Gemini CLI automatically redacts potential secrets from environment variables when executing tools (such as shell commands). This "best effort" redaction applies to variables inherited from the system or loaded from .env files. Default Redaction Rules: By Name: Variables are redacted if their names contain sensitive terms like TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, KEY, AUTH, CREDENTIAL, PRIVATE, or CERT. By Value: Variables are redacted if their values match known secret patterns, such as: Private keys (RSA, OpenSSH, PGP, etc.) Certificates URLs containing credentials API keys and tokens (GitHub, Google, AWS, Stripe, Slack, etc.) Specific Blocklist: Certain variables like CLIENT_ID, DB_URI, DATABASE_URL, and CONNECTION_STRING are always redacted by default. Allowlist (Never Redacted): Common system variables (for example, PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TERM, LANG). Variables starting with GEMINI_CLI_. GitHub Action specific variables. Configuration: You can customize this behavior in your settings.json file: security.allowedEnvironmentVariables: A list of variable names to _never_ redact, even if they match sensitive patterns. security.blockedEnvironmentVariables: A list of variable names to _always_ redact, even if they don't match sensitive patterns. json { "security": { "allowedEnvironmentVariables": ["MY_PUBLIC_KEY", "NOT_A_SECRET_TOKEN"], "blockedEnvironmentVariables": ["INTERNAL_IP_ADDRESS"] } }

conditions: when executing tools (such as shell commands).

name: GEMINI_CLI_HOME
description: Specifies the root directory for Gemini CLI's user-level configuration and storage. By default, this is the user's system home directory. The CLI will create a .gemini folder inside this directory. Useful for shared compute environments or keeping CLI state isolated. Example: export GEMINI_CLI_HOME="/path/to/user/config" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GEMINI_CLI_HOME="C:\path\to\user\config")

name: GOOGLE_API_KEY
description: Your Google Cloud API key. Required for using Vertex AI in express mode. Ensure you have the necessary permissions. Example: export GOOGLE_API_KEY="YOUR_GOOGLE_API_KEY" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_API_KEY="YOUR_GOOGLE_API_KEY").

name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
description: Description: The path to your Google Application Credentials JSON file. Example: export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/your/credentials.json" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="C:\path\to\your\credentials.json")

name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION
description: Your Google Cloud Project Location (for example, us-central1). Required for using Vertex AI in non-express mode. Example: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION="YOUR_PROJECT_LOCATION" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION="YOUR_PROJECT_LOCATION").

name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
description: Your Google Cloud Project ID. Required for using Code Assist or Vertex AI. If using Vertex AI, ensure you have the necessary permissions in this project. Cloud Shell note: When running in a Cloud Shell environment, this variable defaults to a special project allocated for Cloud Shell users. If you have GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set in your global environment in Cloud Shell, it will be overridden by this default. To use a different project in Cloud Shell, you must define GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT in a .env file. Example: export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID").

conditions: If using Vertex AI, ensure you have the necessary permissions in this project.

name: GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL
description: Overrides the default base URL for Gemini API requests (when using gemini-api-key authentication). Must be a valid URL. For security, it must use HTTPS unless pointing to localhost (or 127.0.0.1 / [::1]). Example: export GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL="https://my-proxy.com" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL="https://my-proxy.com")

conditions: when using gemini-api-key authentication).

name: GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION
description: Specifies the API version to use for Gemini API requests. When set, overrides the default API version used by the SDK. Example: export GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION="v1" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION="v1")

conditions: When set, overrides the default API version used by the SDK.

name: GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL
description: Overrides the default base URL for Vertex AI API requests (when using vertex-ai authentication). Must be a valid URL. For security, it must use HTTPS unless pointing to localhost (or 127.0.0.1 / [::1]). Example: export GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL="https://my-vertex-proxy.com" (Windows PowerShell: $env:GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL="https://my-vertex-proxy.com")

conditions: when using vertex-ai authentication).

name: NO_COLOR

name: OTLP_GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
description: Your Google Cloud Project ID for Telemetry in Google Cloud Example: export OTLP_GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" (Windows PowerShell: $env:OTLP_GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID").

name: SEATBELT_PROFILE
description: Switches the Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) profile on macOS. permissive-open: (Default) Denies operations by default, confining writes to the project folder (and a few other folders, see packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-permissive-open.sb) while allowing broad file reads and network access. restrictive-open: Declines operations by default, allows network. strict-open: Restricts both reads and writes to the working directory, allows network. strict-proxied: Same as strict-open but routes network through proxy. : Uses a custom profile. To define a custom profile, create a file named sandbox-macos-.sb in your project's .gemini/ directory (for example, my-project/.gemini/sandbox-macos-custom.sb). DEBUG or DEBUG_MODE (often used by underlying libraries or the CLI itself): Set to true or 1 to enable verbose debug logging, which can be helpful for troubleshooting. Note: These variables are automatically excluded from project .env files by default to prevent interference with gemini-cli behavior. Use .gemini/.env files if you need to set these for gemini-cli specifically.

conditions: if you need to set these for gemini-cli specifically.

description: Route sandboxed network traffic through an HTTP proxy. Fields: url (required), username (optional), password (optional). On Linux and macOS the proxy is cooperative (not strictly enforced); Windows enforces it.

description: Custom status line display. type: must be "command". command: path to an executable script that receives session JSON on stdin and prints status content to stdout. padding: optional number of left-padding spaces. refreshInterval: optional integer number of seconds (1–2147483) to re-run the command on a timer instead of only on events; omit it to refresh only when the session state changes. If the command fails to spawn, exits non-zero, or fails to receive the status JSON on stdin, the CLI logs a warning once per continuous failure episode and leaves the status line blank instead of failing silently. Run with --log-level all to see the underlying error detail.

name: Goal tracking observer

name: Memory recall observer
description: A background observer that surfaces a note from local project memory relevant to the next reply.
when_to_use: Let durable project facts reach a turn without asking for them.

conditions: On by default. Rollout gates and the settings file can disable it.

notes: Each enabled observer makes its own model calls, so the default set of four adds token usage.

name: Skill recall observer
description: A background observer that surfaces a project skill the task should load first.
when_to_use: Let a relevant skill reach a turn without naming it yourself.

conditions: On by default. Rollout gates and the settings file can disable it.

name: Verification observer
description: A background observer that checks the agent ran the work it claims it finished.
when_to_use: Catch a turn that reports success without running the check.

conditions: On by default. Rollout gates and the settings file can disable it.

notes: An observer never answers for you: it proposes, a reconciler decides, and only an accepted proposal reaches the main agent.

name: subagent
description: A child agent the lead session spawns for one bounded task, optionally in an isolated Git worktree.
when_to_use: Split a job into bounded, independently verifiable tasks that would otherwise contend for the same files.
when_not_to_use: Keep the work on one agent when the steps are strictly sequential.
notes: One agent tree executes eight agents at once by default, including the root agent; an unconfigured ultra root uses 64.
Cancellation is cooperative: a cancelled child that never reaches a checkpoint keeps running, and one mid-write finishes that write.
An isolation request is never silently downgraded to the shared checkout.

name: muse
description: Launch an interactive Muse Code session in the current project directory.

notes: The judge is part of the approval layer, not a separate layer. Introduced in 0.2.1 as automatic approval pre-screening.

name: --approval-mode
description: Select the approval policy for tool calls with side effects: on-request, untrusted, or never.

examples.explanation: Stop for review on any shell stage with no matching allow rule.

Save a local script as a named workflow.

name: --json

when_to_use: Consume a headless run's progress from a script rather than reading prose.
when_not_to_use: It is a headless-only flag; the interactive TUI does not accept it.

name: --max-model-steps
description: Cap the number of model steps in a headless run.

examples.explanation: Stop a stuck task from looping indefinitely.

when_to_use: Bound the cost and duration of an unattended run.

conditions: Hitting the limit ends the run with exit code 1.

name: --model
description: Choose the model for the run. The default model is muse-spark-1.2.

examples.explanation: Start a session on a specific model.

when_to_use: Pin a run to a model other than the default.
notes: Since 0.2.1 --model accepts any model id; an unknown id uses assumed metadata instead of being rejected.

name: --no-session-log
description: Run without retaining the session event log.

examples.explanation: Run an interactive session with no retained log.

when_to_use: Run a session you do not want recorded on disk.
when_not_to_use: It forfeits resume, trajectory export and reattach, automatic session naming and peer messaging, rewind, and retained workflow recovery.

name: --out
description: Write the export to a chosen path.

examples.explanation: Write the session trajectory to run.json.

when_to_use: Update a saved workflow in place after editing its script.

name: --prompt-file
display_name: Read the prompt from a file
description: Read a headless run's prompt from a file instead of an argument.

examples.explanation: Run a long prompt kept in version control.

name: --reasoning-effort
description: Trade latency for depth with none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or ultra. The default is high.

examples.explanation: Lower reasoning depth for a faster session.

examples.explanation: Use the premium-precision tier for a hard headless task.

when_to_use: Match reasoning depth to the difficulty of the task.

conditions: The Meta provider does not accept none; other providers can support it.

notes: ultra is a client-side setting that maps to each provider's highest supported tier and can make Muse Code delegate more aggressively.

examples.explanation: Export one retained session's trajectory.

examples.explanation: Validate an enterprise-managed configuration document.

when_to_use: Check a centrally administered configuration document before rolling it out.

name: muse exec
description: Run one prompt to completion without a terminal UI, for scripts and CI pipelines.

name: muse export
description: Write a retained session's full event log to a JSON document for audit or replay.

examples.explanation: Export one session's trajectory to a JSON file.

when_to_use: Audit a run after the fact, or feed a recorded trajectory into a replay check.

conditions: Requires a retained session log.
The export document embeds the CLI version that produced it.

description: Write a single AGENTS.md into the current directory to seed the project's agent rules.

Creates no other files and does not change settings.json.

examples.explanation: Clear the stored browser session and stored key.

when_to_use: Sign out of Muse Code on a shared or retired machine.

description: Reopen a retained session in the interactive UI and continue it.

examples.explanation: Open the interactive resume picker for retained sessions.
Continue a session branched earlier with /fork.

when_to_use: Continue an interrupted or forked session with its event log replayed.
when_not_to_use: Use muse exec --session-id to continue a job non-interactively; muse resume always opens the UI.

conditions: Requires a retained session log; unavailable for sessions started with --no-session-log.

description: Command group for listing, inspecting, enabling, installing, validating, and importing skills.

examples.explanation: Enable a skill for this project.

when_to_use: Turn on a discovered skill for a project or for your account.

description: Import skills from another agent's skill directories.

examples.explanation: Import skills authored for Claude Code.

description: Show the definition and metadata of one skill by id.

description: Install a skill directory at the chosen scope.

examples.explanation: Install a local skill directory for your account.

when_to_use: Add a skill you authored or received to your account or a repository.

name: muse skills list
description: List every skill available to Muse Code across built-in, user, project, and plugin sources.

examples.explanation: Show every skill and the source it loads from.

when_to_use: Check which skills a workspace actually exposes before you invoke one.

examples.explanation: List saved project and user workflows.

when_to_use: Confirm a saved workflow is discoverable before a session tries to run it.

conditions: Requires a build that includes the workflow script engine and access to the staged WorkflowTool rollout.
Trust the workspace in a session first, then exit before listing project workflows.

name: muse workflows recover
description: Restart the remaining child work of a retained workflow run after a process restart.

examples.explanation: Reuse committed results and restart only the remaining child work.

when_to_use: Continue a workflow whose owning process exited before the run finished.
when_not_to_use: Wait for the current attempt to finish or fail first; one workflow owner runs at a time.

conditions: Requires a workflow-engine-enabled build and the retained session identifiers.

name: muse workflows save
description: Save a JavaScript workflow script at project or user scope so a session can run it by name.

examples.explanation: Write .agents/workflows/review-change.js for the repository.

when_to_use: Keep an orchestration pattern your team repeats.
when_not_to_use: Saving does not parse or run the JavaScript; syntax errors surface when the workflow launches.

conditions: Requires a build that includes the workflow script engine and access to the staged WorkflowTool rollout.
The source must be a regular, nonempty UTF-8 file no larger than 512 KiB.

notes: Workflow names use lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, and hyphens, start with a lowercase letter or digit, and run to 64 characters.

name: .muse/hooks.json
description: Hooks committed to a repository at the project root.
when_to_use: Share lifecycle automation with everyone who clones the repository.
when_not_to_use: Only add hooks whose commands you have read; a hook runs through your shell outside the sandbox and approval.
notes: Project hooks run only after you trust the project folder, and take effect as soon as you trust it since 0.2.1.
A malformed project or managed hook file contributes no handlers from that source and produces a startup warning.

name: ~/.config/muse/settings.json
description: User settings for model defaults, terminal UI, tools, MCP servers, hooks, runtime capabilities, and telemetry.
when_to_use: Set machine-wide defaults you do not want to repeat per session.
when_not_to_use: A missing file is fine; create it only when you have something to set.
notes: The file must set "schema_version": 1. Omitting the key fails every command at startup with malformed settings file.

name: Tools > Session messaging
description: Turn local session-to-session messaging on or off. On by default.
when_to_use: Coordinate independent live sessions with handoffs, review requests, and status updates.
when_not_to_use: A peer message cannot approve a tool call, grant consent, or change permissions; treat it as unverified data.

conditions: Availability depends on the session-messaging rollout gate.
Connects eligible interactive sessions for the same user on the same Unix machine only.

notes: A preference change applies on the next Muse Code launch. Messages carry plain text up to 8,192 bytes.

name: Tools > Workflows
description: Choose whether Muse Code may propose workflows: auto, explicit, or off.
when_to_use: Let Muse Code propose a workflow for workflow-scale work, or require you to ask.

conditions: Requires a build that includes the workflow script engine and access to the staged WorkflowTool rollout.

notes: The setting applies immediately to the current session.

name: agents.execution_capacity
description: The number of agents one tree can execute at once, from 1 through 64. The default is eight, including the root agent.
when_to_use: Raise or lower how many child agents run in parallel.
when_not_to_use: A spawn attempted when the tree is full is rejected.
notes: An unconfigured ultra root uses 64. Every descendant shares the same root-tree capacity.

name: hooks
description: A first-class block in the settings file defining machine-wide hooks.
when_to_use: Run your own automation on lifecycle events across every project.
when_not_to_use: User hooks run from your own settings without a project-trust step, so review what they execute.

name: managed_hooks_path
description: A pointer to a file of centrally administered hooks.
when_to_use: Administer hooks centrally across a fleet of machines.
when_not_to_use: Managed hooks run without a project-trust step, so whoever controls the file controls what executes.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.args
description: Arguments passed to a stdio MCP server.
when_to_use: Pass configuration to a stdio server on its command line.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.command
description: The executable for a stdio MCP server.
when_to_use: Point a stdio server at its binary.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.enabled
description: Whether the server is active.
when_to_use: Keep a server declared but switched off.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.env
description: Environment variables for a stdio MCP server.
when_to_use: Supply credentials or settings a stdio server reads from its environment.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.framing
description: Optional message framing for a stdio server.
when_to_use: Match a stdio server that expects non-default framing.
when_not_to_use: A non-default framing value on streamable_http fails validation.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.headers
description: Headers sent to a streamable_http MCP server.
when_to_use: Authenticate to a remote MCP endpoint.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.mode
description: Whether a server is required or optional. The default is required.
when_to_use: Let a run continue when a non-essential server is unavailable.
when_not_to_use: If a required server fails to start, the whole run aborts.
notes: Optional servers that fail at startup no longer spam the transcript as of 0.2.1.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.transport
description: The server transport: stdio or streamable_http.
when_to_use: Choose between a local child process and a remote HTTP endpoint.

name: mcp_servers.<name>.url
description: The endpoint for a streamable_http MCP server.
when_to_use: Connect to a remote MCP endpoint over HTTP.

name: runtime_capabilities
description: A map that toggles runtime capabilities such as the background observer agents.
when_to_use: Turn an observer agent off when its extra model calls are not worth the token usage.

name: schema_version
description: The settings file schema version, which must be 1.
when_to_use: Include it in every settings.json you create.
when_not_to_use: Omitting it fails every command at startup with malformed settings file; an unrecognized value fails with unsupported settings schema version.

name: show_reasoning
description: Commit the model's full reasoning into the transcript. Off by default.
when_to_use: Keep the model's reasoning in the session record.
notes: It is independent of the live one-line reasoning summary in the status row, which is on by default.

name: CODEX_HOME
description: Point Muse Code at the Codex skill directory it discovers at $CODEX_HOME/skills.
when_to_use: Share one Codex skill library with Muse Code.
when_not_to_use: A user preference and rollout gate can disable foreign personal skill roots.
notes: Muse Code falls back to ~/.codex/skills when CODEX_HOME is unset.

name: META_API_KEY
description: Provide a Meta API key so Muse Code can authenticate without the browser sign-in flow.
when_to_use: Authenticate in CI, a script, or a Meta Managed Account that cannot use browser sign-in.
when_not_to_use: muse logout does not unset an exported META_API_KEY; remove it from your shell or secret store separately.
notes: Muse Code uses META_API_KEY if set, then a stored key, and only then a stored browser session.

name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
description: Root the user skill directory Muse Code discovers at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muse/skills.
when_to_use: Keep account-wide skills outside the default configuration location.

name: PermissionRequest
description: An action requests approval.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when an action requests approval.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: PostCompact
description: Context compaction has finished.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when context compaction has finished.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: PostLLMCall
description: A model call has returned.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when a model call has returned.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: PostToolUse
description: A tool call has finished.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when a tool call has finished.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: PreCompact
description: Context compaction is about to run.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when context compaction is about to run.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: PreLLMCall
description: A model call is about to be made.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when a model call is about to be made.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: PreToolUse
description: A tool call is about to run.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when a tool call is about to run.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when the session terminates in an orderly way.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.
notes: SessionEnd is observational: its output cannot block termination, inject context for a later request, or stop the session.

name: SessionStart
description: A session starts.
when_to_use: Bind a shell command to run when a session starts.
when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.
notes: Muse Code discovers and validates hooks at session startup. There is no active muse hooks command family or per-hook trust command.

when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.
