when_not_to_use: A hook's command runs directly through your shell, outside the sandbox and approval that govern the agent's own tools.

name: .agents/AGENTS.md
description: The third instruction file Muse Code checks at each directory level.
when_to_use: Keep agent configuration together under .agents/ rather than at the repository root.

name: .agents/memory/MEMORY.md
description: The index of committed project memory, with one Markdown file per topic beside it.
when_to_use: Record durable, project-specific facts: deployment procedures, why a workaround exists, a service's unusual behavior.
when_not_to_use: Treat a repository's MEMORY.md as a prompt-injection surface; it loads even in an untrusted workspace.
notes: At session start Muse Code injects MEMORY.md plus the paths, not the contents, of up to 48 other memory files.

name: .claude/CLAUDE.md
description: The last instruction file Muse Code checks at each directory level.
when_to_use: Reuse a repository's existing Claude Code configuration directory.

name: AGENTS.md
description: The project's agent rules, discovered from the workspace root up to the nearest .git boundary.
when_to_use: Record conventions the agent should follow in this repository.
when_not_to_use: Project rules load only after you trust the workspace.
notes: At each directory level Muse Code checks AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, then .claude/CLAUDE.md, and the first existing file wins for that level.
Project rules win over user rules, and among project files the deeper file wins.

name: CLAUDE.md
description: A Claude Code instruction file Muse Code reads when no AGENTS.md exists at that directory level.
when_to_use: Reuse instructions already written for Claude Code without duplicating them.

name: mcp_servers.<name>
description: Declare an MCP server in the settings file with a stdio or streamable_http transport.
when_to_use: Connect external tools to the agent through the Model Context Protocol.
when_not_to_use: MCP tools are not sandboxed; an MCP server runs outside the filesystem and network sandbox.
notes: Settings accept the standard mcpServers key as well since 0.2.1, and configuration across multiple files and scopes merges consistently.

name: headless
description: One prompt run to completion without a UI, for scripts and CI.
when_to_use: Run the agent from a pipeline where nobody is watching the terminal.

name: interactive
description: The terminal UI for a back-and-forth session with slash commands, approvals, and live status.
when_to_use: Work with the agent conversationally and approve actions as they come up.

name: Allow once
description: Run the held shell stage one time only; Muse Code saves no rule.
when_to_use: Approve a one-off command you do not want to grant standing permission for.

name: Always allow in this workspace
description: Save an allow rule for this command's prefix, scoped to this workspace root.
when_to_use: Stop re-approving a command you run constantly in one project.
when_not_to_use: You cannot save an interpreter prefix such as python, bash, or node as a broad allow.
notes: Prefix rules apply by specificity, and a deny rule always overrides an allow rule whatever the specificity.

name: Workspace trust
description: Trusting a workspace root lets Muse Code load that project's skills, rules, and hooks.
when_to_use: Work in a repository you control and want project configuration to apply to.
when_not_to_use: Leave a checkout you do not control untrusted; its AGENTS.md, rules, skills, and hooks are attacker-controlled instruction.
notes: Committed project memory under .agents/memory/ loads even in an untrusted workspace, unlike skills, rules, and hooks.

name: enabled
description: Full outbound network access from sandboxed commands.
when_to_use: Run a task whose network use you already trust, such as a dependency install in a container.

name: never
description: Nothing stops for approval; the sandbox alone contains what runs.
when_to_use: Run unattended where the sandbox is the intended boundary.
when_not_to_use: Do not use it where the sandbox is unavailable or disabled.

name: on-request
description: The default approval mode: recognized, non-dangerous parsed shell stages pass, while dangerous or external-execution patterns stop for review.
when_to_use: Work interactively with guardrails that stay out of the way for safe commands.
notes: Dangerous patterns include destructive removal forms and ripgrep options that can launch helper processes, such as -z, --search-zip, --pre, and --hostname-bin.

name: proxy-only
description: The default network policy: outbound connections are approved per destination, and the first connection to a new host, port, or protocol stops for review.
when_to_use: Let a task reach the network while keeping each new destination visible.

name: restricted
description: No network access from sandboxed commands.
when_to_use: Run a task that has no legitimate reason to reach the network.

name: untrusted
description: A stricter mode in which any shell stage with no matching allow rule stops for review.
when_to_use: Review every unmatched shell stage on code you do not control.
notes: It escalates shell execution only. File reads and in-workspace write_file and edit_file writes still pass in any mode.

description: Run a shell command from the composer instead of sending a prompt to the model.

examples.explanation: Run a shell command without leaving the session.

when_to_use: Check repository state or run a quick command mid-session.
when_not_to_use: Shell commands still run under the approval policy and the OS sandbox.
notes: Documented in the release notes, which record that hooks triggered by ! shell commands are durably recorded and survive resume and export.

description: Open the command palette in the composer and filter it as you keep typing.

examples.explanation: Open the command palette and filter the command list.

when_to_use: Find a command without memorizing its name.
notes: Skill slash commands are highlighted while you type as of 0.2.1.

name: Alt+Enter
description: Hold the typed text for the next turn instead of injecting it into the current one.

examples.explanation: Queue an instruction for after the current turn finishes.

when_to_use: Line up the next instruction while the agent is still working.

name: Alt+V
description: Start or stop voice input, transcribing speech into the composer.

examples.explanation: Dictate a prompt instead of typing it.

when_to_use: Dictate a long prompt.

conditions: option-V on macOS. Voice is enabled by default on macOS and off by default on Linux.

name: C
description: Cancel the selected workflow from the control-room run list.

examples.explanation: Cancel the selected workflow run.

when_to_use: Stop a workflow that is no longer worth its token usage.

conditions: Available in the /workflows control room, which requires the workflow engine build and rollout.

name: Ctrl+C
display_name: Interrupt, clear input, or leave a side chat
description: Interrupt from an empty composer, clear the input when it holds text, and return to the main thread from a side conversation.

examples.explanation: Interrupt the current turn from an empty composer.

when_to_use: Leave a side conversation, or interrupt without reaching for Esc.

name: Ctrl+L
description: Clear the terminal screen without clearing the session.

examples.explanation: Clear the screen while keeping the session.

when_to_use: Tidy a crowded terminal without resetting the conversation.
notes: Described in the 0.2.1 release notes, which record a fix for redraw artifacts.

name: Ctrl+N
description: Move to the next message in the rewind picker.

examples.explanation: Move down the rewind picker.

when_to_use: Navigate the rewind picker without the arrow keys.

name: Ctrl+P
description: Move to the previous message in the rewind picker.

examples.explanation: Move up the rewind picker.

when_to_use: Navigate the rewind picker without the arrow keys.

name: Enter
description: Submit text that is injected into the turn in progress; the agent applies it on its next step.

examples.explanation: Steer a running turn without waiting for it to finish.

when_to_use: Correct the agent's direction mid-turn.

name: Esc
description: Cancel the current turn. On an empty composer it instead retracts the most recently queued instruction.

examples.explanation: Interrupt the current turn.

when_to_use: Stop a turn that is going the wrong way.
when_not_to_use: Esc stops the turn only. It does not stop background terminals or subagents; use /stop for those.
notes: Only the newest eligible queued item is retractable at a time.
Interrupting a turn automatically pauses an unfinished goal.

name: Esc Esc
description: Press Esc twice in quick succession from an idle, empty composer to open the rewind picker.

examples.explanation: Open the rewind picker to branch from an earlier message.

when_to_use: Take the conversation in a different direction from an earlier message.
when_not_to_use: Rewind changes conversation history only; it does not restore, revert, or delete workspace files.

conditions: Available only in interactive sessions with session logging enabled.
Starts only from the idle main conversation with an empty composer.

notes: There is no /rewind slash command.
The picker labels each prior input Exact, Review required, or Blocked.

name: P
description: Pause or resume the selected workflow run from inside the control room.

examples.explanation: Pause a running workflow.

when_to_use: Hold a run while you inspect an intermediate result.

conditions: Available in the /workflows control room, which requires the workflow engine build and rollout.

name: R
display_name: Open a result or restart a child
description: Open the result of a completed workflow from the run list, or restart the selected running child inside a run.

examples.explanation: Open the result of a completed workflow.

when_to_use: Read a finished run's output, or restart a child that stalled.
when_not_to_use: R is not a general retry for completed or failed children.

conditions: Available in the /workflows control room, which requires the workflow engine build and rollout.

name: Space
description: Close the workflow control room from any level.

examples.explanation: Close the workflow control room.

when_to_use: Return to the conversation; the workflow keeps running in the background.

conditions: Available in the /workflows control room, which requires the workflow engine build and rollout.

name: Tab
display_name: Add a note to a clarifying answer
description: Add an optional free-text note to a clarifying question the agent asked.

examples.explanation: Add a free-text note to a clarifying answer.

when_to_use: Explain a choice the offered options do not capture.
notes: Answers to clarifying questions are conversational input. They grant no filesystem, shell, network, or approval authority.

name: X
description: Skip the selected running child agent inside a workflow run.

examples.explanation: Skip a running child agent.

when_to_use: Drop a child whose result you no longer need.

conditions: Available in the /workflows control room, which requires the workflow engine build and rollout.

name: .agents/skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md
description: A skill committed to a repository, shared with anyone who clones it.

examples.explanation: Author a project skill the whole team gets on clone.
Check the skill before committing it.

when_to_use: Package a repeatable workflow the agent should load on demand in this repository.
when_not_to_use: Project skills load only after you trust the workspace.
notes: Muse Code also scans repo-local .codex/skills and .claude/skills, and user skills in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muse/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills, and $CODEX_HOME/skills.

name: /grill-with-docs
description: Run the same decision-forcing interview and write the settled decisions into your project docs.

examples.command: /grill-with-docs Pressure-test the transfer design and record decisions
examples.explanation: Turn interview answers into durable project knowledge.

when_to_use: The interview produces decisions worth keeping beyond the transcript.
when_not_to_use: Give the project a home for durable decisions first, or the skill has nowhere to write.
notes: The extending page calls this playbook /grill-and-record while the cookbook documents it as /grill-with-docs. Run /help to see the name your build exposes.

name: /grilling
description: Interview you one decision-forcing question at a time until the design is sharp.

examples.command: /grilling Pressure-test the transfer and overdraft design
examples.explanation: Have the agent play skeptic one question at a time.

when_to_use: You have a rough idea and want its assumptions pressure-tested before you build.
when_not_to_use: It is explicit-invocation only; Muse Code does not run it because a request looks underspecified.
notes: The extending page calls this playbook /grill while the cookbook documents it as /grilling. Run /help to see the name your build exposes.

name: /plan
description: Ground a plan in your files, name the key decisions, save it to .agents/plans/, and stop for approval before any code changes.

examples.command: /plan Add a transfer operation with overdraft protection
examples.explanation: Produce a decision-complete plan and stop for approval.

when_to_use: The work has decisions to make before code: an API to design, a migration to sequence, a PR to split.
when_not_to_use: It is explicit-invocation only; task complexity alone does not trigger it, and it does not plan ordinary implement, fix, or refactor requests.
notes: The extending page lists this bundled playbook as /plan, matching the cookbook.

name: /taste
description: Apply a flat checklist of visual defaults to avoid, so generated frontend UI stops looking machine-made.

examples.command: /taste Build the landing page from the README
examples.explanation: Generate UI with the anti-slop checklist applied.

when_to_use: You are generating a UI and want to avoid the purple gradient, centered hero, three-card grid look.
when_not_to_use: It never prescribes a specific look; an explicit request from you overrides the checklist.

name: /clear
description: Start a fresh session and wipe the terminal scrollback.

examples.explanation: Start a fresh session and clear the screen.

when_to_use: Begin unrelated work with a clean screen.
when_not_to_use: Neither /new nor /clear changes on-disk memory or rules.

name: /compact
description: Replace earlier model-visible history with a generated summary to reclaim context room.

examples.explanation: Summarize prior context to reclaim room.

when_to_use: Continue a long task that is filling the context window.
when_not_to_use: It is lossy for the model's context; export the transcript first if you need the verbatim record.
notes: Muse Code also compacts automatically when context fills. A manual /compact never counts against the auto-compaction budget, and since 0.2.1 it runs in the background.

name: /copy
description: Copy the markdown of the last completed response to the clipboard.

examples.explanation: Copy the last response to the clipboard.

when_to_use: Move an answer into a pull request, an issue, or a document.

name: /effort
description: Change the reasoning effort mid-session.

examples.explanation: Raise or lower reasoning effort without restarting.

when_to_use: Spend more reasoning on a hard step and less on routine ones.

name: /export
description: Write the on-screen conversation to a text file, or the full session log to JSON.

examples.explanation: Write the on-screen conversation to a .txt file.
Write the full session log to JSON with secret-shaped strings scrubbed.

when_to_use: Keep a durable record of a session for review or audit.

name: /fork
description: Branch a new session from the current session's latest stable point.

examples.explanation: Branch a new session and leave the current one running.

when_to_use: Explore an alternative direction without disturbing the running session.
notes: The source session stays active and unchanged, and the fork does not take over your view. Continue it later with muse resume <fork-id>.

name: /goal
description: Set, show, revise, pause, resume, or clear the objective the runtime holds the agent to.

examples.command: /goal Ship the migration with green tests
examples.explanation: Set the objective for a multi-turn task.
Restart goal tracking after an interrupt paused it.

when_to_use: Hold the agent to an outcome across many turns.
notes: Interrupting a turn with Esc automatically pauses an unfinished goal.
The runtime prompts the agent to report_progress if it goes about 10 model steps without one.

name: /help
description: Show the full set of commands available in this workspace.

examples.explanation: List every command available in the current session.

when_to_use: Discover which commands a workspace actually exposes, including skills.

name: /keymap
description: Show the keyboard shortcuts available in the interactive session.

examples.explanation: Show the session's keyboard shortcuts.

when_to_use: Look up a shortcut without leaving the session.

name: /login
description: Reopen the sign-in options: a browser sign-in or a pasted Meta API key.

examples.explanation: Reopen the sign-in options from a running session.

when_to_use: Switch credentials, or sign in after starting a session unauthenticated.

name: /loop
description: Schedule a recurring prompt as a cron job, using a shorthand interval or a 5-field cron expression.

examples.explanation: Run the /run-tests skill every ten minutes.
Run a prompt on weekdays at 9am local time.

when_to_use: Repeat a check on a cadence while you work on something else.
when_not_to_use: An occurrence that lands during an active run is skipped, not queued or replayed.
notes: With no cadence it defaults to every ten minutes, and recurring jobs auto-expire after 7 days.
There is no dedicated loop-monitor panel; a loop is an ordinary scheduled job managed with the agent's cron tools.

name: /models
description: Switch the session's model mid-session.

examples.explanation: Switch models without restarting the session.

when_to_use: Move a running session to a different model.

name: /name
description: Show the current session name, or assign one.

examples.explanation: Show the current session name.
Give this session a stable name other sessions can address.

when_to_use: Give a session a stable name so peers can message it.
notes: After normalization a name is 3-32 ASCII characters, starts with a lowercase letter, uses lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, and avoids a trailing or doubled hyphen. all, self, and current are reserved.

name: /new
description: Start a fresh session and keep the terminal scrollback on screen.

examples.explanation: Start a fresh session without clearing the screen.

when_to_use: Begin unrelated work while keeping the previous output visible.
when_not_to_use: It resets the conversation, context, token counts, goal, and tasks; use /compact to reclaim room instead.

name: /recap
description: Render a short summary of what happened since the last recap.

examples.explanation: Summarize recent activity after stepping away.

when_to_use: Catch up on a long-running session you left unattended.
when_not_to_use: It needs new activity to summarize and runs between turns, not during one.
notes: A recap is a summary cell only. It does not change the model's context.

name: /resume
description: Pick a retained session in this workspace and continue it.

examples.explanation: Pick a retained session to continue.
Resume the most recent session in this workspace.

when_to_use: Continue work from a previous session in the same workspace.
when_not_to_use: It is unavailable inside a side conversation; return to the main thread first.

name: /settings
description: Open the settings surface for tool, model, and interface preferences.

examples.explanation: Open settings to change tool and interface preferences.

when_to_use: Turn voice, workflows, or session messaging on or off.

name: /side
description: Start a short parallel conversation seeded from the main session without changing the main thread.

examples.explanation: Open a side conversation.

examples.command: /side How does the retry policy work?
examples.explanation: Ask a side question without adding it to the main history.

when_to_use: Ask something that should not enter the main conversation's history.
when_not_to_use: Only one side conversation can be open at a time, and /side, /fork, /new, /clear, and /resume are unavailable inside it.
notes: Press Ctrl+C to return to the main thread, which Muse Code restores exactly.

name: /status
description: Show a summary card for the current session.

examples.explanation: Show the session summary card.

when_to_use: Check what the current session is configured to do.
notes: Redesigned as a summary card in 0.2.1. The command is currently described only in the release notes.

name: /stop
description: Cancel applicable background tasks and terminals.

examples.explanation: Stop background tasks and terminals left running.

when_to_use: Clean up background work after interrupting a turn with Esc.
when_not_to_use: It does not blanket-cancel direct subagents; manage those through /tasks.

name: /subagents
description: Open the subagent view for running and completed descendants.

examples.explanation: See which child agents are running and what they produced.

when_to_use: Follow a fan-out job across its child agents.

name: /tasks
description: Open the drawer for background tasks and direct subagents, with controls for the selected row.

examples.explanation: Open the Tasks drawer to manage background work.

when_to_use: Manage a long shell command, a monitor, or a direct subagent.

name: /upgrade
description: Open Accounts Center in your browser to change or cancel a Muse Code subscription.

examples.explanation: Open Accounts Center to change your plan.

when_to_use: Move between the Everyday, High, and Power usage plans.

conditions: Requires a Meta Account and a Muse Code subscription flow available in your region.

name: /usage
description: Show usage and cost totals for the session, labeled in USD.

examples.explanation: Show session usage and cost totals.

when_to_use: Track what a long session is spending before it grows further.
notes: Costs are labeled explicitly as USD since 0.2.1. The command is currently described only in the release notes.

name: /voice
description: Show voice status or toggle voice diagnostics.

examples.explanation: Show whether voice input is available.

when_to_use: Diagnose why dictation is not working.
when_not_to_use: /voice inspects state only; turn voice on or off in /settings, not with /voice on.

conditions: Voice is enabled by default on macOS and off by default on Linux.

name: /workflows
description: Browse active and completed multi-agent workflow runs, with phases, progress, usage, and results.

examples.explanation: Open the workflow control room.

when_to_use: Watch or steer a multi-agent run: pause, resume, cancel, skip, or restart a child.

conditions: Requires a build that includes the workflow script engine and access to the staged WorkflowTool rollout.
The public aarch64-apple-darwin package does not include workflow-script-engine-v8, so workflows are unavailable in that artifact.

name: .agents/workflows/<name>.js
description: A reusable JavaScript workflow saved at project scope and loaded once when a session starts.
when_to_use: Keep an orchestration pattern your team repeats: parallel groups, dependent stages, and a final synthesis.
when_not_to_use: Commit the file before another clone can discover it, and restart a session saved after it launched.

conditions: Requires a build that includes the workflow script engine and access to the staged WorkflowTool rollout.
Project workflows load after you trust the workspace.

notes: A workflow can call up to 1,000 child tasks over its lifetime; the local active-child limit is CPU-derived and capped at 16.
A completed script must return a JSON-serializable value.
